title: Microbially driven iron redox chemistry unlocks phosphorus reservoirs in oxygenated soils
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Biological phosphorus (P) mobilization is generally attributed to proton- and ligand-driven dissolution of mineral P, enzymatic hydrolysis of organic P, and, under anoxic conditions, reductive release of phosphate from Fe(III) minerals. Here, we show that extracellular metabolites released by diverse Gram-positive bacteria sustain Fe(III) reduction under oxic conditions, releasing mineral-associated phosphate. The resulting Fe(II) reacts with O
                    2
                    to generate reactive oxygen species that activate organic P. This redox pathway was observed across diverse aerobic bacteria and agricultural soils and increased plant-available P. These findings establish aerobic microbial Fe redox chemistry as a previously overlooked route for returning otherwise inaccessible P to bioavailable pools, with implications for reactivating legacy P in agricultural soils.

title: Phosphorylation-dependent ATPase activity regulates subunit shuffling dynamics in cyanobacterial circadian clock proteins
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Protein complexes are essential for cellular functions, with their dynamics increasingly recognized as key regulatory elements. In the cyanobacterial circadian clock, the KaiC hexamer is highly dynamic, undergoing phosphorylation-dependent monomer shuffling that synchronizes individual oscillators. However, the molecular mechanism of monomer shuffling is not fully understood. Here we combine a chromatography-based method with single-molecule fluorescence microscopy to quantify subunit exchange in the hexamerization domain of KaiC (KaiC-CI) and in full-length KaiC. We show that ATPase activity is essential for monomer shuffling. Through quantitative modeling of experimental data, we found that adenosine triphosphate (ATP) hydrolysis at two independent monomer–monomer interfaces disassembles a KaiC-CI hexamer into two oligomers. Two complementary oligomers from two different hexamers can rapidly reform a mixed hexamer. Mechanistically, ATP hydrolysis induces unstable, shuffling-competent states in hexamers, while nucleotide exchange stabilizes them, suppressing shuffling. The balance between these two processes quantitatively explains the relationship between shuffling rate and ATPase activity across KaiC mutants observed in our experiments. Applying this model to full-length KaiC revealed that phosphorylation of the KaiC-CII domain modulates shuffling primarily by affecting the nucleotide exchange rate in the CI domain. This establishes a feedback loop where CII phosphorylation alters CI ATPase activity, which in turn controls subunit exchange to synchronize CII phosphorylation across the KaiC hexamer population. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework linking ATPase-driven subunit exchange to the robustness of circadian clocks, with implications for activation-coupled dynamics in other molecular machines.

title: Vegetation decay enhances terrestrial nitrous acid emissions through nitrate reduction
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Photolysis of nitrous acid (HONO) drives ozone and secondary aerosol formation, yet its sources remain poorly constrained. We identify HONO emissions from decaying aboveground plant residues as a previously overlooked plant-derived component of terrestrial HONO emissions. Field observations and dual-isotope (
                    15
                    N–
                    18
                    O) tracing reveal that HONO arises mainly from nitrate reduction within decomposing plants. We integrated global datasets on vegetation nitrate, litter decomposition, soil, and climate to estimate HONO emissions from vegetation decay at 1.1 ± 0.1 Tg N y
                    −1
                    . This substantially narrows the long-standing uncertainty in HONO budget. This plant-mediated pathway extends the soil-atmosphere paradigm to soil-plant-atmosphere framework. Moreover, we identify emission hotspots and drivers, assess their climate-driven shifts, and propose region-specific mitigation strategies. These findings uncover a missing link between terrestrial nitrogen cycling and atmospheric reactivity, highlighting biogeochemical controls on air quality.

title: Quantifying (de)mixing of disordered proteins in molecular dynamics simulations
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Biomolecular condensates control the spatial and temporal organization of cellular biochemistry. Their architectures often arise from complex, multicomponent mixtures governed by weak, multivalent interactions between intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) of proteins. However, current approaches lack generalizable metrics to determine whether IDRs will mix or segregate within condensates. Here, we present a domain decomposition method (DDM) that accurately determines phase concentrations without identifying condensate interfaces. When tested against 399 IDR simulations, the DDM recovers dense- and dilute-phase concentrations within 1% agreement of established surface-based methods. By calculating spatial variances to map three-dimensional organization, this approach successfully distinguishes homogeneous mixing from surface enrichment, core–shell architectures, and complete segregation. Applying this continuous metric to 2,068 binary mixtures of 32 distinct IDRs, we demonstrate that physicochemical similarity strongly promotes mixing. Hydrophobic IDRs mixed promiscuously across all partner chemistries, whereas charged sequences mixed in a way highly sensitive to charge complementarity, forming the most stable condensates as net charge approached zero. Compared with experimental networks, our IDR-only simulations predicted the partitioning preferences for 10 of 13 proteins, with discrepancies accurately isolating cases where colocalization strictly requires RNA or folded domains. Quantifying mixing in this way provides a robust and reproducible method for predicting IDR interactomes and understanding the composition of complex cellular condensates.

title: Precursor-engineered lithiation kinetics enable low-temperature synthesis of Li–Ni–O positive electrode materials
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
High-nickel cathodes provide high capacity in lithium-ion batteries; however, their slow lithiation reactions require a prolonged high-temperature hold during synthesis which is directly responsible for high manufacturing cost. Here, we report that the precursor morphology and crystallinity can be engineered to regulate the nucleation and growth of the layered phase at temperatures as low as 575 °C. We use nanosheets of NiO and Ni(OH)
                    2
                    with high specific surface areas to maximize the contact area between Li and Ni precursors and to shorten Li
                    +
                    diffusion lengths. Highly crystalline NiO seeds early and uniform layered phase nucleation at low temperatures. Preheating Ni(OH)
                    2
                    to NiO at 300 °C maintains the large surface area and yields a higher layered fraction with limited lamellae coarsening. Preheating at 500 °C produces more crystalline NiO seeds that promote the synchronous Ni oxidation and cation ordering upon layered phase formation to deliver higher discharge capacity and better rate capability than conventionally synthesized LiNiO
                    2
                    . In contrast, along the hydroxide-based route, in situ generated Li
                    2
                    CO
                    3
                    disrupts wetting and hampers lithiation, ultimately trapping lithium within a disordered rocksalt intermediate. This work demonstrates that precursor morphology, crystallinity, and processing temperature control lithiation kinetics, providing broad guidance for energy-efficient synthesizing advanced oxide battery cathodes.

title: Ctf4 chaperones parental histones to preserve epigenetic memory
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Faithful transmission of chromatin states through cell division requires symmetric transfer of parental histones to daughter strands, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we identify the replisome scaffold Ctf4 as a bona fide histone chaperone that directly orchestrates parental histone transfer to preserve epigenetic inheritance. We show that the N-terminal domain (NTD) of Ctf4 harbors a specific histone-binding motif (HBM) embedded within its intrinsically disordered linker region. This HBM engages the DNA-binding surface of histone H3 and, in concert with Spt16 and Mcm2, transiently tethers parental histone hexamer onto Tof1 at the advancing replisome, priming them for subsequent transfer to nascent DNA. Disrupting Ctf4-HBM severely compromises parental histone sequestration, misdirects their recycling away from the lagging strand, and causes substantial loss of gene silencing at heterochromatic loci. Our findings establish Ctf4 not merely as a structural scaffold, but as a central chaperone at the replication fork that actively governs symmetric partitioning of parental histones, thereby ensuring the fidelity of epigenetic memory through successive cell divisions.

title: Frontispiece: Active‐Site Photothermal Energy Utilization in PET Depolymerization
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: Photothermal catalysis depends not only on heat generation, but also on the efficiency of energy delivery to active sites of the catalyst (Pd). In the Research Article e2844693, Yiming Bu, Jingliang Li, and co-workers reveal the critical role of the local thermal environment at active sites in PET depolymerization. These findings highlight effective active-site temperature, rather than bulk temperature, as a key factor for photothermal catalysis.

title: Interploidy massively increases meiotic crossovers in pericentromeric recombination deserts
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Meiotic recombination reshuffles genetic diversity through reciprocal DNA exchanges between chromosomes known as crossovers. In most eukaryotes, crossovers are highly constrained in both frequency and distribution, leaving large genomic regions with little or no recombination. A notable exception is the
                    Brassica
                    AAC allotriploid hybrid obtained from a cross between allotetraploid
                    Brassica napus
                    (AACC) and diploid
                    Brassica rapa
                    (AA), which exhibits elevated recombination and crossover formation near centromeres. Here, we generated a CCA allotriploid hybrid from a cross between
                    B. napus
                    and
                    Brassica oleracea
                    (CC), and subsequently produced AAC allotriploids by crossing the CCA hybrid with
                    B. rapa
                    . Both CCA and AAC allotriploids exhibit similar meiotic deregulation, demonstrating that this phenomenon is not restricted to AAC hybrids. Both systems displayed a marked increase in crossover frequency within normally low-recombining chromosome regions, reaching 9.4-fold in AAC and 13.4-fold in CCA allotriploids. Alternating CCA and AAC allotriploids efficiently reshuffled both
                    B. napus
                    subgenomes within only two generations. Using genetic mapping and cytogenetics, we further identified homoeologous exchanges. Remarkably, crossovers occurring on chromosomes involved in homoeologous associations exhibited a more pronounced redistribution toward nonrecombining regions than those on homologously paired chromosomes. Moreover, the frequency of homoeologous associations varied with the diploid progenitor genotype, indicating that genetic factors controlling homoeologous recombination already exist in
                    Brassica
                    diploids. Altogether, our results identify allotriploidy as a simple and powerful strategy to unlock recombination deserts, which harbor 21% of total resistance gene analogs, and provide insights into its potential role in allopolyploid evolution, adaptation, and speciation.

title: Evidence for patterns of colonization risk in the nationwide hospitalized patient network in France
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Patient movement within and between hospitals creates a complex hospital network that facilitates the spread of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria and contributes to healthcare-associated infections. Yet most national-scale studies infer spread from aggregated hospital-to-hospital patient sharing, leaving patient-to-patient contact pathways and the role of routine patient mobility in shaping colonization risk poorly characterized. Using France’s 2023–2024 national hospital-discharge data, we reconstructed a temporal patient-based network of 10.4 million patients across 1,408 acute-care hospitals, comprising 326.6 million overnight ward colocation interactions. We simulated colonization over 365 d on the observed day-by-day temporal network using a stochastic susceptible–colonized–susceptible model, with a mean colonization duration of 180 d. We used national carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) surveillance data to calibrate differences in transmission risk across clinical settings. Across 2,000 simulations initiated on randomly selected dates in 2023, we calculated patient-level colonization probabilities and summarized risk across patients’ residential areas, wards, and hospitals. We further assessed hospital-level consistency between simulated risk and recorded CPE occurrence. Simulated risk was highly heterogeneous across patients and care settings. When mapped by place of residence, hospital-associated colonization risk showed strong spatial clustering in both urban and rural areas. Multivariable regression analyses identified patient- and hospital-level characteristics associated with heterogeneity in simulated colonization risk. Sensitivity analyses varying initial seeding and colonization duration showed that relative risk patterns remained highly stable. This nationwide framework shows how patient mobility and ward colocation patterns can reveal patterns of hospital-associated colonization risk and could support pathogen-specific surveillance and intervention evaluation.

title: Airborne microbial diversity over Greenlandic and Antarctic plateaus reflects divergent atmospheric connectivity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The polar plateaus are among the most remote environments on Earth. Despite their extreme conditions, these cold deserts on the Greenland and Antarctic Ice Sheets harbor microbial life in snow, ice, and air. However, knowledge of polar airborne microbiomes remains scarce and methodological differences have hindered bipolar comparisons. Here, we present a systematic survey of airborne bacterial and eukaryotic communities across Greenlandic and Antarctic Plateaus, using standardized sampling and genetic techniques, coupled with atmospheric physics and advanced statistical analyses. We found that Antarctic airborne communities are characterized by low diversity and high homogeneity, whereas Greenlandic communities are richer, more variable, and more connected to coastal-marine zones. Our results indicate that atmospheric isolation, together with short-term atmospheric variables, is associated with differences in the microbial biogeography of each Plateau. Compared with Antarctica, the Greenlandic Plateau is more frequently influenced by air masses from outside the plateau over long timescales and exhibits more variable short-term air back-trajectories, reflecting enhanced microbial dispersal and diversity. These findings highlight the potential of polar plateaus as observational platforms for airborne microbial diversity, where sustained and temporally resolved sampling could help assess variations in community composition associated with atmospheric circulation and anthropogenic influence under global change.

title: Cognitive diversity and majority rule
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Societies rely on groups–boards, panels, committees, and representative bodies–to make important decisions for good reason: overwhelming evidence shows groups usually make more accurate choices than individuals. The predominant logic for group accuracy rests on reasoning formulated in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, which states that if voters receive independent and equally accurate generated signals, majority rule produces decisions that i) are more accurate than the average voter, ii) improve in individual accuracy and iii) group size, and iv) approach perfect accuracy as group size becomes large. An alternative logic based on interpreted signals explains the accuracy of majority rule as arising from the aggregation of diverse mental models. Group accuracy results from the same state of the world being classified differently by different people. In this framework, the set of possible group accuracies can be characterized conditional on average individual accuracy and average pairwise diversity. Majority rule groups are only guaranteed to outperform their members when diversity is high. Using data from a variety of empirical settings, along with simulations of a minimal nearest-neighbor model, we find much stronger support for the predictions of the interpreted signals framework than for the standard generated signals model. We further show empirical evidence for a diversity–accuracy paradox, in which more diverse groups are less accurate unless average individual accuracy is nearly constant across groups. Our findings have important implications for group composition and institutional and organizational design as well as for the potential gains from deliberation.

title: Ultrasound Rechargeable Bioelectronics With Acoustic Metamaterial‐Enhanced Triboelectric Energy Harvesting
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Wireless transcutaneous energy transfer to deep‐tissue bioelectronic implants remains challenging for long‐term autonomous bioelectronic operation because tissue attenuation limits the available acoustic excitation. Here, we present a proof‐of‐concept ultrasound rechargeable bioelectronic platform that integrates spatially confined acoustic energy delivery, energy harvesting, power management, and programmable electrical stimulation. A non‐resonant, transmissive acoustic metamaterial reshapes the incident ultrasound wavefront to form a localized field in the receiving region. The platform couples this acoustic structure with a compliant thin‐film triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) for energy harvesting in a fluidic environment. An on‐board power conditioning circuit regulates the harvested energy to support recharging and controlled electrical pulse delivery. In ex vivo evaluations using a layered porcine‐tissue configuration, approximately 3.5 min of ultrasonic recharging supports nearly 16 h of programmed pulse generation into a 5 kΩ surrogate load, corresponding to an acoustic charging duty cycle of 0.36%. The stored energy also powered electrical pulses that evoked repeatable limb movement in ex vivo frog preparations. These results demonstrate a system‐level strategy for ultrasound‐rechargeable bioelectronics, providing a basis for future implantable neuromodulation systems.

title: Correction to “A Robust Au─C≡C Functionalized Surface: Toward Real‐Time Mapping and Accurate Quantification of Fe2+ in the Brains of Live AD Mouse Models”

title: A Climate‐Adaptive Window Enabling All‐Day Anti‐/Deicing and Dynamic Thermal Management
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Transparent anti‐/deicing materials have traditionally focused on maximizing solar harvesting to achieve efficient ice mitigation under cold conditions. However, this approach can introduce overheating risks during warm periods, creating a challenge in balancing anti‐/deicing and thermal management. Here, we report a climate‐adaptive window consisting of a spectrally selective optical switch, a hybrid Joule‐heating and a highly transparent superhydrophobic coating. Guided by an energy‐balance framework for full spectrum design, the window simultaneously achieves high luminous transmittance (65.2%), strong near‐infrared absorption (76.1%), and large solar modulation capability (36.0%), enabling dynamic thermal regulation while preserving robust anti‐/deicing functionality. The synergistic interplay of photo‐electrothermal heating, thermal retention, and superhydrophobicity extends icing delay by 11‐fold and realizes rapid all‐day deicing at −20°C. Under hot conditions, the thermochromism reduces the average indoor temperature by 15.2°C, substantially reducing building cooling demand and boosting greenhouse seedling biomass relative to conventional configurations. By integrating solar modulation with transparent anti‐/deicing functionality, this work paves the way for the development of next‐generation climate‐adaptive windows.

title: A Mesohydrous Metallic Gel for Imperceptible Electrophysiology
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Imperceptible skin electronic interfaces for bidirectional communication are essential for next‑generation healthcare and human–machine interfaces. The long‑standing absence of an ideal interfacing material has made it challenging to achieve high‑quality bidirectional electrophysiology without disturbing innate perception. Inspired by the human stratum corneum's mesohydrous state, we report a metallic stratum corneum (MSC): a synthetic mesohydrous gel reinforced with a silver nanowire network. MSC achieves > 10

Its porous ultrathin architecture enables multidimensional imperceptibility (tactile, mechanical, thermal, and vapor‑permeable). MSC records electrophysiology with signal‑to‑noise ratio surpassing commercial gel electrodes, delivers efficient neuromuscular stimulation, and forms high‑resolution electrode arrays for spatiotemporal muscle mapping. By reconciling electronic performance, skin compatibility, and imperceptibility, the mesohydrous gel establishes a promising material platform for next‐generation on‐skin bioelectronics.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Helical mesoporous architectures are attractive for electrochemical energy storage because their curved channels and spiral surfaces facilitate ion transport and interfacial charge transfer. However, their synthesis has traditionally relied on chiral templates or complex assembly procedures, limiting structural tunability and compositional flexibility. title: Medium‐Entropy Metallene Enables Sequential Hot‐Carrier Nanocatalytic Triaptosis Induction for Suppressing Tumor Growth and Metastasis
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Triaptosis, a newly recognized cell death modality driven by endosomal dysfunction and persistent vacuolization, holds promise for tumor therapy. However, its clinical translation has been hindered by the lack of spatiotemporally controllable strategies to disrupt endosomal homeostasis. Herein, we engineer ultrathin PdCuCo medium‐entropy metallene catalysts (PCC MEMCs) as a new class of sono‐activatable catalytic biomaterials that induce triaptosis for tumor therapy. Upon ultrasound irradiation, lattice oscillations in PCC MEMCs generate non‐equilibrium hot carriers that execute two synergistic catalytic functions. These high‐energy hot carriers directly drive interfacial electron transfer with H
                    2
                    O and O
                    2
                    to produce hydroxyl radicals and superoxide anions, with sufficiently energetic carriers further converting triplet oxygen to singlet oxygen. Simultaneously, these hot carriers accelerate the intrinsic enzyocatalytic reactions by lowering surface adsorption barriers and enhancing charge transfer. This sequential nanocatalysis triggers a massive oxidative burst and substantial depletion of antioxidants, leading to VPS34 oxidation, PI(3)P depletion, and disruption of early endosomal processing. Consequently, persistent vacuolization and membrane collapse induce triaptosis, effectively suppressing tumor growth and metastasis. Collectively, this work establishes a sono‑activatable hot‑carrier sequential nanocatalytic paradigm, offers a distinct nanotherapeutic strategy against tumors via triaptosis induction, and broadens the biomedical scope of medium‐entropy metallenes toward sonocatalytic therapy.

title: Chiral Bobbers in the Room‐Temperature Magnet Co8Zn10Mn2
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Chiral bobbers are three‐dimensional magnetic solitons that emerge near surfaces of chiral magnets with bulk‐type Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction. They can be regarded as skyrmion strings terminated by a Bloch point inside the material. So far, chiral bobbers have been observed only at cryogenic temperatures. Here, we report the direct observation of chiral bobbers in  over a broad temperature range, including room temperature. Using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy combined with micromagnetic simulations, we identify a previously unreported nucleation pathway in which skyrmion strings transform into chiral bobbers under an applied magnetic field. We also demonstrate that chiral bobbers on opposite surfaces can be coupled to form double‐bobber states. These findings establish chiral bobbers as room‐temperature magnetic textures and identify their role in the nucleation pathways of topological magnetic solitons.

title: Dynamic Commercial Silicones Toward Sustainable, Task‐Reconfigurable Suction Gripping
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Silicone suction cups are widely used in industrial automation for scalable, high‐throughput handling, yet conventional designs are restricted to limited geometries. Advancing toward gripping is essential to transition robotics from single‐task execution to versatile handling across dynamic environments but presents a fundamental materials challenge: balancing the properties of on‐demand geometric reconfigurability with operational strength and elasticity. Existing universal grippers typically utilize composite materials that couple shape adaptation and gripping operation within a single cycle, introducing critical performance trade‐offs in force, speed, and preload requirements while adding structural complexity that together hinder broad industrial adoption. To address this, we establish a versatile post‐fabrication strategy that transforms commercial silicone thermosets into dynamic silicone materials via catalyst‐mediated exchange of intrinsic siloxane bonds. This enables scalable transformation of industrial suction cups to reconfigurable grippers that reconfigure shapes at elevated temperatures while preserving high gripping performance via thermosetting properties at ambient temperatures. We demonstrate an all‐silicone, hierarchically structured suction gripper combining a reconfigurable load‐bearing body with a compliant sealing interface towards sustainable, task‐reconfigurable gripping, ensuring infrastructure compatibility while delivering rapid suction actuation (50 ms) following thermal reconfiguration (e.g., ∼30 min at 140°C), efficient load capacity (27 kPa), and zero‐preload attachment across diverse environments.

title: Ultrastable Chromium Pyrazolate Polyhedra With Amorphization‐Enhanced Microporosity for Corrosive Guest Capture

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The chemical stability of porous coordination solids is commonly rationalized using hard–soft acid–base (HSAB) considerations, which have largely excluded chromium(III)‐pyrazolate architectures owing to their incompatibility and the kinetic inertness of Cr(III). Here, we report the first porous chromium(III) pyrazolate metal–organic polyhedron. The material exhibits extraordinary chemical robustness, remaining chemically intact over a pH window spanning 13.7 units (pH < 0 to 13). The protonation tendency of azolate ligands is largely suppressed upon coordination to Cr(III), leading to resistance to acidic environments. Remarkably, even after amorphization induced by prolonged boiling in water (Cr(III)‐MOP‐A), the discrete Cr–pyrazolate cages persist, as evidenced by XPS and EXAFS, accompanied by an approximately twofold increase in the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface area. title: Self‐Calibrating Fluorescence‐Exclusion Microfluidic Platform for 3D Topographic Profiling of Living Cell Monolayers
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Cell monolayers are active living matter whose three‐dimensional (3D) architecture and mechanical remodeling regulate tissue function, yet fast and continuous topographic monitoring remains difficult. Here, we present fluorescence exclusion microscopy for monolayers (FLEXOM), a microfluidic platform combining multilayer micropillar arrays with negative‐staining optics to convert wide‐field images into self‐calibrated 3D height maps. Geometry‐anchored cavities allow in‐frame self‐calibration at confluence, correcting global intensity variations shared by sample and reference regions. FLEXOM enables longitudinal 3D profiling from isolated cells to confluent sheets with sub‐second temporal resolution, sub‐micrometer temporal height precision, and multiday biocompatibility and operational stability. FLEXOM reveals two distinct anisotropic signatures. First, monolayers show distinct cell type‐dependent vertical thickness profiles despite comparable lateral footprints. Two vertical descriptors, mean height and within‐cell height standard deviation, distinguish cell types more accurately than nine two‐dimensional (2D) lateral descriptors. Second, under acute osmotic shock, diverse confluent cell monolayers exhibit geometrically anisotropic vertical–lateral remodeling. Under hypotonic stimulation, projected area changes lag behind height changes. Consistent with this lag, cyclic hypotonic–isotonic switching at 3‐min intervals produces predominantly vertical remodeling with limited cycle‐dependent lateral changes. Our work provides a high‐resolution 3D profiling tool and a framework for axis‐resolved analysis of topographic responses in active living matter.

title: Task‐Oriented Co‐Design of Optoelectronic Synaptic Devices: From Physical Mechanisms to System Integration
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Optoelectronic synaptic devices integrate optical sensing, state storage, and conductance modulation, offering high bandwidth, ultrafast response, and low energy consumption. These capabilities enable the development of energy‐efficient, scalable intelligent vision systems with rich synaptic plasticity, making optoelectronic synaptic devices one of the most promising approaches for overcoming the limitations of conventional von Neumann computing architectures. However, existing studies often evaluate device performance and synaptic functions under disparate structures and operating conditions, obscuring the relationships among physical mechanisms, device design, and task requirements, and limiting the establishment of generalizable design principles. This Review presents a task‐oriented framework that connects biological functions and application requirements with physical mechanisms, multilevel hardware design, and system integration. We first summarize biological synaptic and retinal functions and define key evaluation metrics and task requirements. We then discuss major operating mechanisms and strategies for coordinated optimization across materials, interfaces, device structures, and arrays. Representative applications are further reviewed, together with key challenges, including device stability, array uniformity, large‐scale integration, peripheral‐circuit overhead, and standardized benchmarking. By shifting the focus from isolated performance optimization toward cross‐level co‐design, this Review provides design guidelines for reproducible, scalable, and energy‐efficient optoelectronic neuromorphic hardware.

title: Single‐Device Bidirectional Photonic Synapses: From Polarity Switching to Adaptive Neuromorphic Computing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Neuromorphic vision requires hardware capable of integrating sensing, memory, and computation with bidirectional information processing. Single‐device bidirectional photonic synapses (BPS), which enable positive and negative photoresponses within the same physical element, provide a compact platform for adaptive photonic computing. However, the diverse architectures, regulation strategies, and physical mechanisms reported for BPS have hindered systematic understanding and quantitative comparison. Here, we establish a unified Structure–Regulation–Mechanism–Function (S–R–M–F) framework to organize single‐device BPS from device architecture and polarity regulation to physical mechanisms, synaptic functions, quantitative benchmarks and neuromorphic applications. We further distinguish physical photoresponse polarity from its functional interpretation in synaptic computing and highlight key considerations including energy consumption, reproducibility, variability, and system‐level scaling. Finally, we identify the transition from empirically observed PPC–NPC switching toward predictive, deterministic, programmable and reproducible operation as a key direction for future BPS development, with physics‐informed modeling and closed‐loop control offering promising routes toward adaptive photonic neuromorphic hardware.

title: AI‐Driven Intelligent ECM‐Mimetic Hydrogel Scaffolds for Brain Organoid Engineering
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Brain organoids are increasingly used for scalable modeling of human neurodevelopment and disease, but their reproducibility and translational value remain limited by reliance on ill‐defined matrices such as Matrigel. Although Matrigel provides several brain‐relevant features, including soft, viscoelastic, and non‐fibrillar properties, its composition is poorly defined, batch‐variable, and difficult to tune in a standardized manner. Considering the physicochemical characteristics of the native brain extracellular matrix (ECM), brain organoid culture requires ECM‐like materials that reproduce brain‐specific mechanical, transport, and signaling cues rather than merely providing 3D support. This review presents a rational framework for engineering intelligent ECM‐mimetic hydrogel scaffolds for advanced brain organoid culture. It summarizes key features of the native brain ECM and introduces material rationality as the systematic selection and engineering of hydrogels according to brain‐specific biological, physical, and translational design requirements. The review also highlights how artificial intelligence (AI) can navigate high‐dimensional material design spaces through surrogate modeling, digital twins, and closed‐loop optimization informed by multi‐physics and multi‐omics feedback. Ultimately, AI‐driven scaffold design may enable more reproducible, mature, and scalable brain organoid models.

title: Reconstructing Structural Dynamic Cooperativity Suppresses Conduction Loss in Linear Aliphatic Polymer Dielectrics at Elevated Temperatures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics show increased conduction loss at elevated temperatures as thermally activated structural fluctuations modulate electronic states and facilitate charge transport. We examine how aromatic side groups with different π‐electron delocalization affect structural dynamic cooperativity and charge transport. Side‐group modification alters intermolecular interactions and local dynamic constraints, shifting long‐range cooperative motion to localized heterogeneous fluctuations. This transition coincides with reduced collective structural fluctuations and improved local electronic‐state stability, consistent with suppressed phonon‐assisted carrier transport. As a result, the furan‐modified polymer exhibits a statistical electronic energy fluctuation descriptor of 0.132 eV and nearly two orders of magnitude higher volume resistivity. It achieves a discharged energy density of 8.38 J cm
                    −3
                    at 120°C, approximately 45 times that of pristine polymer while maintaining a charge‐discharge efficiency above 90%. It also retains an efficiency above 93% over 5 × 10
                    5
                    charge‐discharge cycles at 200 MV m
                    −1
                    . Although the higher glass transition temperature of the furan‐modified polymer may also contribute to its performance near 120°C, its advantage is already evident at 25°C and 80°C, well below the glass‐transition regime. This work highlights structural dynamic cooperativity as a descriptor linking molecular dynamics and charge transport in linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics.

title: Multiscale Design of Strong and Tough Gelatin Hydrogels for Biomedical Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Gelatin, a natural polypeptide derived from partial hydrolysis of collagen, possesses excellent biocompatibility, biodegradability, inherent cell‐adhesive properties, and abundant functional groups for chemical modification. These intrinsic advantages have established gelatin hydrogels as promising platforms for diverse biomedical applications. Despite these merits, conventional gelatin hydrogels exhibit insufficient strength and toughness, restricting their use in mechanically demanding and long‐term biomedical scenarios. Recent advances have addressed these limitations through multiscale engineering of molecular interactions, network topology, domain or interface organization, and higher‐order structures. These approaches substantially enhance strength and toughness, while providing additional control over other coupled mechanical responses. This review outlines the design principles and multiscale strategies for strong and tough gelatin hydrogels, summarizes recent progress in their biomedical applications, and discusses key challenges and future directions toward mechanical regulation and clinical translation.

title: An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells
source: Nature
abstract: All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. Here we incorporate a redox-converted molecule of p-aminobenzohydrazide (ABH) into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) that neutralizes PSS acidity, heals Sn4+ defects, and generates a dipole passivation effect upon oxidation. During the preparation of Sn-Pb perovskites, ABH suppresses interfacial oxidation by reducing Sn4+ defects and converts to p-aminobenzaldehyde (ABD), which suppresses photogenerated hole-induced Sn2+ oxidation, aligning energy levels for efficient hole extraction. The in situ redox-converted molecule stabilizes the buried interface during both device fabrication and operation, reduces non-radiative recombination and enhances stability. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
source: Nature
abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

title: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
source: Nature
abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut–brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop—a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut–brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states.

title: Excitonic electrically tunable metaatoms for visible light
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Phase-gradient metasurfaces shape optical wavefronts through arrays of optical nanoantennas acting as metaatoms. While dynamic tunability forms a major frontier in this area, direct electrical switching of metaatoms operating in the visible has remained challenging. Here, we present an exciton-based metaatom that is electrically tunable and operates in the visible. Its function originates from an excitonic absorption band of a dedoped conjugated polymer, which together with low background permittivity induces optical metallicity in the visible. This allows anisotropic nanostructures to exhibit polarization-dependent optical response through localized surface exciton-polariton resonances, rather than plasmons or dielectric Mie resonances. This function can be fully switched off through reversible doping by small bias potentials, which turns off the exciton-induced metallicity. Our study details the mechanism of these metaatoms and demonstrates their use in electrically tunable phase-gradient metasurfaces for visible light, including erasable and rewritable holograms. This work thereby establishes a class of electrically switchable exciton-based metaatoms and expands the design space of dynamic visible metaoptics.

title: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Northern Hemisphere snow cover retreat poses substantial climate risks, but large uncertainties in Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) hinder accurate projections of future evolution. We develop a monthly emergent constraint based on historical warming trends, which strongly correlate with ablation-season (May–October) snow cover loss. This constraint reduces inter-model variance by 17.0–58.4% under different emission scenarios and rectifies raw CMIP6 snow-loss biases. Constrained projections reveal that under the higher-emission scenario (SSP5-8.5), winter snow cover retreats in arid regions from the 2030 s, and Arctic summers become snow-free by the 2040 s. By mid-century, mid-latitude spring and autumn snow cover disappears, with arid and semi-arid regions approaching year-round snow-free conditions and humid regions losing 1–4 months of seasonal snow cover. Under the most sustainable scenario (SSP1-2.6) snow disappearance is delayed by 7.1–34 years relative to SSP5-8.5 across vulnerable regions and months. Overall, our constraint narrows projection uncertainty by 0.95–11.91 years, delaying projected disappearance by 0.01–2.65 years in transitional months while advancing it by 0.51–4.15 years in midsummer, providing refined month-specific baselines for climate risk assessments.

title: Ultrafast cellulose nanocrystal production from diverse lignocellulosic biomass
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: The production of cellulose nanocrystals conventionally relies on hazardous chemicals and energy-intensive purification, limiting their sustainable and scalable manufacture. Here we propose a hydrolytic quasi-solvent strategy that enables the rapid extraction of CNCs from microcrystalline cellulose within 15 min, and lignin-containing cellulose nanocrystals directly from untreated biomass within 1 h, with near-closed-loop solvent recycling. Composed entirely of the ionic liquids 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium hydrogen sulfate and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride, the quasi-solvent leverages synergistic ionic interactions to enhance cellulose accessibility, surface functionalization and crystallite dispersion. Meanwhile, the imidazolium cations facilitate lignin removal from raw biomass through localized π–π interactions. Life cycle assessment shows that the recyclable process substantially reduces environmental impacts relative to conventional sulfuric acid hydrolysis and 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl-mediated oxidation, while lowering estimated production costs by 55% and 33%, respectively. By integrating rapid nanocellulose extraction, direct biomass processing and solvent circularity, the present strategy provides a scalable and economically viable route towards resource-efficient lignocellulosic biorefineries.

title: Superspreading droplets for scalable and green perovskite photovoltaics
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Transitioning perovskite solar cells from laboratory demonstrations to commercial production requires minimizing raw material waste while maximizing manufacturing throughput. Although drop-coating is a continuous, potentially waste-free manufacturing route, its sensitivity to substrate surfaces has limited its wider adoption. Here we describe an ink formulation containing driving solvents that amplify outward surface-tension gradients, forcing droplets to rapidly spread over a wide range of materials, including highly hydrophobic surfaces. This superspreading mechanism enables near-complete utilization of the precursor chemicals, while accelerating film-deposition rates by more than 30-fold. Fully drop-coated perovskite solar cells achieved a power conversion efficiency of 26.36% (certified 26.11%). The formulation also preserves the underlying crystallization pathway during scale-up, allowing direct translation to industrially relevant coating techniques. A large-area minimodule fabricated by blade-coating achieved an efficiency of 22.81% over a 54.8 cm2 aperture. By decoupling droplet spreading from substrate surface chemistry, this strategy provides a broadly applicable route to high-throughput, material-efficient perovskite film manufacturing and advances the scalable production of high-efficiency photovoltaics.

title: Molecular-level pre-mixing enables robust high-entropy coating for sodium-ion battery cathodes
source: Matter
abstract: Uniform high-entropy coatings are challenging to construct on sodium-ion layered cathodes because conventional solid-state and wet-chemical routes are intrinsically constrained in achieving multicomponent homogeneity. Here, molecular-level pre-mixing is enabled by a high-entropy Prussian blue analog serving as an “all-in-one” precursor. During reactive annealing, the precursor consumes residual surface alkalis while forming a homogeneous high-entropy interphase, thereby enhancing initial Coulombic efficiency, rate capability, cycling stability, and air stability.

title: Computer vision links electroplated lithium morphology to lithium metal battery performance
source: Matter
abstract: Morphology is critical to materials research, yet its analysis often relies on subjective, qualitative observations that are difficult to quantify. Using lithium metal as a model, this study combines large-area automated microscopy with computer vision to establish quantitative descriptors of metal deposits. These measurements enable objective comparisons of lithium growth in different electrolytes and a combined criterion for rapid electrolyte screening. More broadly, this framework offers a transferable route toward quantitative, reproducible morphology analysis across materials science.

title: Localization of micron-scale lithium polysulfide-rich phases causes anode heterogeneity in lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur batteries

abstract: Kim et al. reveal that concentrated lithium polysulfides form micron-scale, salt-anion-deficient phases in lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur batteries, promoting heterogeneous interphase formation and uneven lithium deposition. Fragmenting these phases with a lithium iodide additive improves anode uniformity and cycling stability, establishing spatial electrolyte heterogeneity as a key consideration for practical batteries.

title: Integration of Mott neurons and spintronic memories for event-driven spiking neural networks
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Spiking neural networks provide energy-efficient, event-driven computing, but separating volatile neuronal dynamics from non-volatile memory imposes costly signal transfer and conversion. Here we demonstrate a hybrid compute-and-store core that directly integrates thermally coupled vanadium dioxide Mott leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to spintronic memory. The neurons require no external resistive or capacitive elements for temporal integration and write their output spikes into either domain-wall racetracks or spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions without amplifiers or analogue-to-digital converters. In racetracks, spike number and amplitude are converted into domain-wall displacement, spatially preserving temporal histories and enabling up to six spikes per processing cycle. Distinct spike trains generated from encoded input patterns produce separable non-volatile states, demonstrating event-based processing and read-out. A network model parameterized by experimental leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics achieves 96.3% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition. Functional coupling of a 500-nm leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to a 100-nm spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junction further establishes nanoscale compatibility. The demonstrated compute-and-store core consumes 51.9 nJ per spike-to-memory conversion, with sub-200-nm vanadium dioxide devices indicating operation near 200 pJ, offering a scalable route towards dense, low-power edge neuromorphic systems for real-time sensory processing.

title: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
source: Nature
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker—ejection fraction—although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

title: An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals
source: Nature
abstract: Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

title: Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
source: Nature
abstract: Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide1,2,3,4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

title: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons
source: Nature
abstract: Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP
source: Nature
abstract: Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

title: Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro
source: Nature
abstract: Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
source: Nature
abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics1,2. Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively2, rare variation remains relatively unexplored1. Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency ACAN) to +11 cm (FBN1) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes (TET1, DTL and IGF2BP2) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects—often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes—and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.

title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
source: Nature
abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956-mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb–seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
source: Nature
abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

title: Climate warming amplifies metabolic imbalance across global lakes
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Lake metabolism remains a critical yet poorly constrained component of the global carbon cycle. Here we integrate satellite observations, climate reanalysis data, free-water measurements derived metabolic estimates and machine-learning approaches to quantify lake metabolism across more than 4000 lakes from 2003 to 2024. We show that global lakes are overwhelmingly net heterotrophic, with ecosystem respiration (ER) exceeding gross primary production (GPP) in approximately 95% of lakes, generating a global metabolic imbalance equivalent to ∼2 Pg C yr−1. Temperature is the dominant control on metabolic variability, and warming stimulates ER more strongly than GPP across most climatic regions. Consequently, climate warming is projected to intensify both the annual mean and intra-annual variability of GPP and ER, leading to an 11% more negative annual net ecosystem production by the end of this century (−2.03 to − 2.26 Pg C yr−1). These findings highlight lake metabolism as an important component of carbon-climate feedbacks.

title: Metal-meets-acid: catalysis for lignin depolymerization
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Lignin, the most abundant renewable aromatic biopolymer on Earth, represents a highly promising feedstock for sustainable chemicals and biofuels. However, the efficient catalytic depolymerization of lignin remains challenging due to its robust interunit linkages and the tendency of reactive intermediates to form irreversible condensates. Acid-metal bifunctional catalysis has emerged as an effective strategy to address these challenges, as the acid sites and metal sites promote bond cleavage while stabilizing intermediates to suppress recondensation. This review focuses on the cooperative mechanisms between acidic sites and metal catalysts during lignin valorization. We examine the specific catalytic functions of these dual active sites, discuss how their bifunctional catalysis enables efficient depolymerization, and summarize recent advances in catalyst design. In the end, we provide perspectives on tuning the spatial distribution and matching degree of dual active sites, offering potential directions for the future development of effective lignin conversion catalysts.
