title: Molar-mass- and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules via iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of α-substituted acrylates
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Free-radical polymerization of simple vinyl monomers enables mass production of widely used polymers, but typically affords products that are poorly defined in molecular size and monomer sequence. Despite advances in precision polymerization, chain growth remains probabilistic, precluding molar-mass- and sequence-defined macromolecules. Here we report photoredox decarboxylative addition of bulky α-substituted acrylates, which enables quantitative addition of single building blocks without oligomerization. The α-acyl radical generated upon acrylate addition is irreversibly deactivated by rapid electron transfer within the photocatalytic cycle. A C(sp3)-centred radical is regenerated only after conversion of the terminal ester into a carboxylic acid and subsequent photoredox decarboxylation. Iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition yields vinyl macromolecules comprising residues identical to the repeat units of conventional vinyl polymers, without inseparable oligomeric impurities. Aperiodic vinyl-residue sequences can be assembled rapidly in continuous-flow reactors, offering a route towards fully automated synthesis of synthetic macromolecules and exploration of their sequence-dependent functions.

title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
source: Nature
abstract: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex1,2. Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools3,4,5,6. Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST (PseCAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution8. However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation9. Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the PseCAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the PseCAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa PseCAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
source: Nature
abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3,4,5,6,7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

title: Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids
source: Nature
abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V−1 s−1 and submillimetre drift lengths—far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection.

title: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis
source: Nature
abstract: Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
source: Nature
abstract: Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of O(1)" role="presentation">O(1){\mathcal{O}}(1) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
source: Nature
abstract: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs)1,2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus1, yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade–TniQ, TnsC and TnsA–TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems.

title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
source: Nature
abstract: Molecular and morphological evidence increasingly supports the view that most East Asian Middle to Late Pleistocene archaic Homo belong to Denisovans1, yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5–42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo, as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo.

title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
source: Nature
abstract: Slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1,2,3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale.

title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
source: Nature
abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot–superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man’s Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron–hole character, but lack topological protection3,4,5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6,7,8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man’s Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
source: Nature
abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease.

title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
source: Nature
abstract: Augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally new ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

title: Dynamic Oxygen Spillover–Structure Feedback in Asymmetric Site Catalysts: Stability Regimes and Design Principles
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Oxygen spillover refers to the transfer of oxygen‐containing species, including adsorbed intermediates and lattice‐derived oxygen, from a donor site/domain to a functionally nonequivalent acceptor through interfacial or connected surface pathways. Despite extensive studies of surface‐confined spillover, its atomic‐scale dynamics in asymmetric multi‐site catalysts remain elusive. This minireview summarizes forward, reverse, and cross‐site oxygen spillover and the key factors regulating these processes. These factors are categorized into intrinsic material properties, including composition, coordination and interfacial structures, and extrinsic operating conditions, such as applied potentials and local electrolyte environments. Moreover, we elaborate on how integrating in situ/operando spectroscopy with theoretical calculations elucidates the structure–activity relationships and dynamic structural evolution at elevated current densities. In particular, drawing on these mechanistic insights, we discuss rational design strategies for asymmetric multi‐atom site catalysts. Specifically, we emphasize how interface engineering, defect control, and self‐optimization methods promote the synergy of spillover effect and structural stability. Finally, we outline the future research direction and emphasize the urgent need to achieve higher space–time resolution in situ characterization and scalable synthesis of uniform asymmetric site catalysts for practical applications.

title: A Novel Metal‐Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework (M‐HOF) Cathode Material for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries (LSBs) are highly promising for next‐generation energy storage devices, yet their practical application is hindered by severe polysulfide shuttling and sluggish sulfur conversion kinetics. Herein, a novel metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF‐21) is constructed and integrated with carbon nanotubes and sulfur as cathode for Li–S batteries. The synergistic combination of hydrogen‐bonding networks and Cu coordination sites enables strong polysulfide anchoring and accelerates sulfur redox conversion. Experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the unique framework structure containing metals and rich abundant hydrogen bonds effectively immobilizes soluble lithium polysulfides, while Cu active centers induce interfacial electronic coupling and optimize the thermodynamic conversion pathway of sulfur species. Benefiting from the adsorption–catalysis synergistic regulation, the HOF‐21/CNT@S cathode exhibits enhanced reaction kinetics, suppressed polysulfide migration, and improved interfacial stability. As a result, the assembled HOF‐21/CNT@S battery delivers excellent long‐term cycling stability with a capacity decay rate of only 0.06% per cycle over 500 cycles at 2 C at room temperature. Moreover, it maintains outstanding low‐temperature adaptability, achieving 76.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at −10°C and 90.6% retention after 200 cycles at −20°C. This work provides a promising strategy for designing advanced cathode materials toward high‐energy‐density Li–S batteries.

ABSTRACT

However, currently reported CBPV predominantly focuses on lead‐containing hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics and the resultant CPL detectors are generally based on bulk crystals, hindering further applications of those materials. ABSTRACT

title: Stress‐Modulated Ionic Transport Limits Composite Cathode Kinetics in Solid‐State Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  High‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) require thick composite cathodes, yet these architectures exhibit heterogeneous reaction distributions that limit their performance. Here, we show that chemo‐mechanical transport switching governs the spatiotemporal lithiation behavior of such electrodes. By combining operando depth‐resolved diffraction with microstructure‐resolved and multi‐scale simulations, we link utilization gradients to the dominant transport pathway and demonstrate that the reversal of reaction fronts between charge and discharge arises from dynamically evolving transport limitations. This switching originates from the coupled reconfiguration of electronic and ionic transport networks during cycling. Particle breathing and interfacial delamination disrupt electronic percolation, whereas the contact‐mechanics model indicates that stress‐field interactions within the solid electrolyte (SE) can limit ionic transport. The model predicts that this suppression depends on the activation volume and elastic properties of the electrolyte and can exceed an order of magnitude as interparticle spacing decreases at high active‐material loadings. Our findings establish a direct link between chemo‐mechanical evolution and transport control in solid‐state cathodes, and highlight the need for SEs with low pressure sensitivity and sufficient mechanical compliance to enable high‐energy ASSB architectures.

title: Photothermal Upcycling of Waste Polyolefins to Ethylene and Propylene Over Waste Plastic‐Derived Carbon Catalysts
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The efficient valorization of polyolefin wastes is challenged by the inertness of C─C bonds and the poor selectivity for olefins, which severely limits the conversion efficiency under mild conditions. Herein, a “treating waste with waste” strategy is proposed by using polypropylene waste derived carbon nanospheres (PP‐C) as the photothermal catalyst for polyethylene (PE) upgrading under focused Xenon light irradiation. Comprehensive characterizations identify that sp
                    2
                    ‐C domains with abundant edge defects of PP‐C serve as the catalytic active sites, which enable outstanding photothermal conversion and facilitate photogenerated charge separation. Theoretical calculations reveal that zigzag edges of sp
                    2
                    ‐structured graphene suppress the recombination of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby the localized electrons at the edge sites effectively weakens C─C bonds on the absorbed reactant and improves the photothermal catalytic efficiency. A remarkable olefin yield of ~60% with approximately 100% PE conversion is achieved within 10 min using PP‐C catalyst under sunlight condition, demonstrating great potential for practical applications. This work not only establishes a sustainable route for plastic valorization but also actively advances an innovative concept for the focused‐sunlight‐drives upgrading of polyolefins.

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Multiferroics exhibiting multiple ferroic orders have gained tremendous attention for decades owing to their intriguing properties and potential applications in future multifunctional devices. However, despite their unique advantages, such as inherent chirality—in contrast to traditional inorganic multiferroics, the design of molecular multiferroics with ferroelectricity and ferroelasticity remains a great challenge. Herein, through oxygen–sulfur (O/S) heavier congener substitution, we successfully designed the first chiral supramolecular ferroelectric–ferroelastic multiferroics [(

Moreover, the O/S substitution induces remarkable chiral amplification, with the dissymmetry factor of the second‐harmonic generation circular dichroism (SHG‐CD) response one order of magnitude larger than that of the parent counterpart. Notably, such an SHG‐CD response can be switched from a high to a low state during the multiferroic phase transition. Our work opens up a new avenue for constructing multiferroic phase transitions in molecular systems and sheds light on the further exploration of chiral supramolecular multiferroics.

title: Chemoselective Electrochemical Ring Cleavage of Naphthols Enabling Structural Diversification
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Structural modification of aromatic frameworks by breaking core C─C bonds is challenging due to their inherent stability. Herein, we introduce an electrochemical dearomative ring‐cleavage method that converts readily available
                    β

Further ring reconstructions provided various carbocycles and heterocycles, highlighting the synthetic versatility of this strategy for the skeletal modification of aromatic frameworks. Mechanistic studies, including intermediate isolation, cyclic voltammetry, and electrode surface analysis, support a stepwise multielectron oxidation process. In this approach, controlled anodic oxidation, cathodically generated nucleophiles, and proton‐coupled electron transfer collectively govern chemo‐ and stereoretentive C─C bond cleavage.

title: A Programmable α‐Aminonitrile Platform for Tunable and Stimulus‐Responsive Hydrogen Cyanide (HCN) Delivery
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Despite increasing evidence that endogenous cyanide participates in cellular signaling, its biological functions remain poorly understood because programmable chemical control over hydrogen cyanide (HCN) delivery has been unavailable. Here we establish a general chemical framework that enables controlled HCN delivery by exploiting the
                    retro

We uncover a predictable structure–reactivity relationship that allows HCN release kinetics to be rationally programmed over more than three orders of magnitude, with half‐lives ranging from 2.9 to 9165 min, primarily through nitrogen‐centered electronic effects with additional steric and conformational modulation. This unified framework further supports multiple modes of molecular control, enabling esterase‐responsive intracellular HCN delivery, ROS‐responsive activation that protects against ischemia–reperfusion injury in both OGD/R cells and MCAO mice, and bioorthogonally triggered HCN generation that suppresses LPS‐induced TNF‐α production in macrophages. Together, these studies establish α‐aminonitriles as an enabling platform that converts cyanide from an experimentally intractable toxic molecule into a chemically programmable signaling entity, providing a molecular foundation for systematic investigation of cyanide biology and its therapeutic potential.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Partial solvation creates interfacial environments that are neither dry solids nor bulk solutions, yet how this intermediate state controls chemical reactivity remains poorly understood. Here, we show that partial solvation at relative humidities far below deliquescence activates unexpected redox chemistry at ionic salt surfaces. Using surface‐sensitive X‐ray spectroscopy, we observe chlorate formation on Arctic sea‐salt crystals and an independent natural salt system following exposure to water vapor, whereas chlorate is absent under dry conditions. First‐principles molecular dynamics simulations reveal strong interfacial electric fields and undercoordinated hydroxide environments, providing physicochemical conditions compatible with charge separation and radical‐mediated oxidation. Our results identify partial solvation as a previously overlooked regime for activating chemical transformations at ionic surfaces and establish partially solvated salt surfaces as distinct reactive environments bridging solid‐state and aqueous‐phase chemistry.

title: Vibrational Strong Coupling of Hydrogen‐Bonding Solvent Modes Modulates Proton Transfer in Wieland–Miescher Ketone Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Vibrational strong coupling (VSC) is emerging as an efficient tool for influencing chemical reactions within an optical cavity. Here, we report the enhancement of ground‐state proton transfer in a multistep Robinson annulation reaction by directly coupling the cavity mode to a selective solvent vibrational mode that is absent in the reactants. Being a hydrogen‐bond‐donating solvent, methanol facilitates proton transfer via a hydrogen‐bonding network, and this proton transfer is further enhanced under VSC. An increase in the product formation upon coupling to the solvent O─H and reactant C═O stretch suggests a unique role of the cavity‐coupling of specific vibrational modes involved in the rate‐determining step (RDS) of the reaction. In this context, the intrinsic intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution (IVR) lifetime of the two modes acts as a key factor in determining the reaction outcome under VSC. Moreover, we find that VSC involving these modes also impacts stereoselectivity, leading to an increased enantiomeric excess (ee). This demonstration of enhanced yield and enantioselectivity under VSC highlights the pivotal role of solvent‐mode coupling in facilitating ground‐state proton transfer through hydrogen‐bonding networks, paving the way for mode‐selective control in complex multistep reactions.

ABSTRACT
                  
                    White phosphorus (P
                    4
                    ) is an indispensable feedstock for organophosphorus synthesis, yet strategies for the controlled manipulation of P
                    4
                    ‐derived polyphosphorus frameworks remain rare. Here, we report a phosphinidene‐mediated strategy that converts P
                    4
                    into a phosphinidene‐bridged hexaphosphane, which functions as a versatile P
                    6
                    platform rather than merely an isolable P
                    4
                    ‐derived framework. This scaffold undergoes controlled P─P bond reorganization, P
                    4
                    release, phosphinidene transfer, heteroelement insertion, and selective derivatization, providing access to phosphorus species spanning P
                    1
                    to P
                    8
                    . Mechanistic studies with water, cyclic(alkyl)(amino) carbenes (CAACs), and N‐heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) reveal dynamic phosphorus‐fragment transfer and carbene‐mediated framework reorganization through phosphinidene‐containing intermediates. Extension to aluminum(I) chemistry affords structurally diverse Al─P clusters that can be converted into value‐added phosphorus products including PH
                    3
                    and PMe
                    3
                    . These results establish phosphinidene‐functionalized polyphosphorus frameworks as promising synthetic platforms for the controlled molecular manipulation of elemental phosphorus.

title: Decoding Direct Regeneration of Spent LiFePO4: From Defect Evolution to Thermodynamic–Kinetic Barrier Engineering
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The rapid growth of LiFePO
                    4
                    (LFP) batteries has made the sustainable recycling of spent cathodes increasingly important for the battery circular economy. Direct regeneration has emerged as the most promising strategy because it preserves the pristine framework, minimizes energy consumption, and maximizes material value. However, the underlying principles governing regeneration remain elusive, as exemplified by the apparent thermodynamic‐kinetic paradox that metallic lithium has been reported to be ineffective for restoring spent LFP, whereas weaker reductants can achieve effective recovery. These observations indicate that regeneration is governed not by thermodynamic driving force alone, but by the coupled effects of electron transfer, ion diffusion, and lattice defects. In this study, we introduce a multiscale defect framework that correlates defect formation energy (Δ
                    H
                    f
                    ), migration barriers (
                    E
                    a
                    ), and electron‐transfer reorganization energy (
                    λ
                    ) with different degradation states of spent LFP. A hypothesis that the dominant barrier evolves with degradation was proposed, enabling failure‐dependent strategies ranging from relithiation and phase‐boundary engineering to defect‐guided upcycling. By transforming regeneration from empirical optimization into rational barrier engineering, this perspective provides a unified understanding of diverse restoration pathways. Finally, emerging challenges, including impurity management, AI‐assisted diagnostics, and closed‐loop materials design, are discussed to guide the development of sustainable battery recycling technologies.

title: Thermodynamic–Kinetic Synergy Enables Neon/Helium Separation in an Anion‐Pillared Metal–Organic Framework
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Separating neon (Ne) from helium (He) remains challenging because both gases are chemically inert and weakly interacting, while classical size‐sieving principles predict faster transport for the smaller He atom. Here we address this challenge with the anion‐pillared metal–organic framework (MOF) Ni(4‐DPDS)
                    2
                    CrO
                    4
                    , whose confined pores combine narrow apertures with electrostatically heterogeneous cavities. This environment provides multiple weak contacts that favor Ne adsorption while producing an inverse diffusional response relative to the expected size trend. At 77 K and 100 kPa, the framework adsorbs 50.63 cm
                    3
                    g
                    −1
                    of Ne but only 0.40 cm
                    3
                    g
                    −1
                    of He in static adsorption, with a kinetic Ne/He selectivity of 113.58. Fixed‐bed experiments afford He with a purity above 99.999%, followed by temperature‐driven recovery of Ne with a purity above 99.7%. The results show that coordinating adsorption thermodynamics with molecular transport offers a route to separating weakly interacting gases beyond equilibrium affinity or classical size sieving alone.

title: d5‐Probed Interlocked Charge‐Structural Disorder Enables Deep Mn3+/Mn2+ Redox Chemistry in Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Mn‐based layered oxide cathodes are attractive for next‐generation rechargeable batteries, owing to their abundant resources and rich redox chemistry, but achieving reversible deep Mn
                    3+
                    /Mn
                    2+
                    redox remains challenging. Herein, we developed an interlocked charge‐structural disorder protocol in P2‐derived Na
                    0.67
                    Fe
                    0.1
                    Mn
                    0.9
                    O
                    2
                    to regulate Mn redox and stabilize discharge voltage. A disordered cation framework is engineered through electronic configuration and atomic rearrangement, where Fe
                    3+
                    (d
                    5
                    , half‐filled) breaks charge periodicity, and rapid quenching prevents structural reordering to eliminate Fe/Mn order. Electron energy‐loss spectroscopy (EELS) reveals suppressed Mn
                    4+
                    /Mn
                    3+
                    charge ordering, which enables extended Mn
                    3+
                    /Mn
                    2+
                    redox as confirmed by soft x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (sXAS). The optimized cathode quenched at 700°C nearly doubles the Mn
                    3+
                    /Mn
                    2+
                    redox contribution within the Mg‐compatible window (1.8–1.6 V vs. Mg
                    2+
                    /Mg) from 15.2% to 29.4%, and it delivers 291.3 Wh kg
                    −1
                    energy density (based on the mass of active cathode) with capacity retention increased from 62.4% to 87.5% over 50 cycles. Mechanistically, the interlocked disorder lowers the migration barrier by flattening the electrostatic‐potential landscape and enhances the thermodynamic driving force for Mn
                    3+
                    /Mn
                    2+
                    by destabilizing Jahn–Teller correlations. This work establishes charge‐state disorder as a versatile design principle for layered oxide cathodes, enabling deep, reversible transition‐metal redox for advanced energy storage.

title: Enantioselective Enyne Cyclization to Thermodynamically Favored Endocyclic Alkenes via a Rhodium‐Migration Relay
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Transition‐metal‐catalyzed addition/cyclizations of electrophile‐tethered alkynes constitute one of the most powerful and broadly applicable strategies for the step‐economical construction of cyclic alkenes. However, these reactions overwhelmingly furnish exocyclic products because the catalytic cycle typically terminates upon kinetically favored ring closure, even though the corresponding endocyclic alkenes are thermodynamically more stable. Herein, we report a catalytic enantioselective arylative cyclization of 1,n‐enynes that directly delivers thermodynamically favored endocyclic alkenes bearing an exocyclic stereogenic carbon center in high yields with excellent chemo‐ and enantioselectivities. Deuterium‐labeling experiments and control studies support a pathway in which the catalytic sequence, rather than terminating after the initial arylative ring closure, continues through a formally circuitous relay of sequential 1,2‐, 1,3‐, and 1,4‐rhodium migrations. This migration relay ultimately transposes the C═C bond to the thermodynamically favored endocyclic position, stereospecifically transfers chirality to the exocyclic stereogenic carbon center, and returns rhodium to its initial carbon attachment site. This work not only establishes a distinct mode of catalytic cyclization but also elucidates the previously unknown mechanism underlying this unusual reactivity.

title: Band‐Filling Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks Through Host–Guest Charge‐Transfer Interactions
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Band‐filling engineering is one of the most rational approaches to controlling the electronic properties of inorganic solids such as cuprates, in which electron/hole doping using heterovalent substitution leads to a rigid‐band shift of the Fermi level. In organic solids, a significant obstacle to accurately predicting electronic properties is the difficulty in maintaining the packing structure during molecular substitution. Here, we utilized a covalent organic framework (COF) in which π‐conjugated electron‐donating molecules are covalently linked to form one‐dimensional pore channels. The introduction of a well‐defined amount of electron‐accepting molecules without disrupting the framework structure enabled the first successful demonstration of the deliberate band‐filling control while elucidating the charge state through various spectroscopic measurements. Enhanced electronic itinerancy facilitated by host–guest charge transfer was evidenced by spectroscopic, transport, and magnetic measurements in support of theoretical calculations. The present study opens a new avenue for exploring more advanced electronic organic solids based on band‐filling engineering.

title: Conformational Locking in Covalent Organic Frameworks Promotes Coupled H2O2 Photosynthesis and Organic Valorization
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer a compelling platform for coupling photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    ) production with organic valorization. However, the practical efficiency remains limited by rapid electron‐hole recombination. Inspired by the conformational rigidity and planar geometry imposed by peptide bonds, we develop a conformational locking strategy that introduces a fused‐ring linker, which restricts backbone rotation and thereby enhances framework planarity and conjugation, affording a series of COFs (TFPPy‐DATMBP, TFPPy‐DABP, and TFPPy‐DAPy) with progressively improved planarity and conjugation. The conformationally locked TFPPy‐DAPy achieves an impressive H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    production rate of 119.8 mmol g
                    −1
                     h
                    −1
                    , with an apparent quantum yield up to 29.14% at 410 nm, while delivering a yield of >98% toward the high‐value imine product. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the conformationally locked TFPPy‐DAPy extends the lifetime of the long‐lived charge‐separated state by approximately 10‐fold to 102.87 ps, compared with 10.34 ps for TFPPy‐DATMBP. This work establishes TFPPy‐DAPy as an efficient photocatalyst for fine chemical co‐production, and provides a generalizable molecular‐level design strategy for developing advanced catalysts across diverse photocatalytic applications.

title: Temporal Fidelity Reveals Transient Dissolution Chemistry at Dynamic Electrocatalyst Interfaces
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Dynamic electrocatalyst dissolution consists of short‐lived, potential‐dependent interfacial events tied to surface redox, reconstruction, and catalysis. Accurate interpretation of these processes requires preserving the temporal link between metal release and electrochemical state, but this link is often lost in electrochemical inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (EC‐ICP‐MS) due to transport‐induced signal convolution. Here we reduce this distortion by using thin‐layer hydrodynamic confinement to improve near‐electrode convective removal. Paired‐pulse dissolution experiments show that two consecutive 2 s dissolution inputs separated by 50 ms remain distinguishable. Cu‐pulse residence‐time‐distribution measurements and computational fluid dynamics further identify electrode‐region convective coverage and near‐electrode flow velocity as key determinants of signal broadening. Applying this temporal fidelity to representative noble‐metal, carbide, nitride, hydroxide, oxide, and single‐atom interfaces under fast cyclic voltammetry reveals distinct dynamic dissolution fingerprints. This approach further resolves weak reoxidation‐associated Ir dissolution from reduced IrO
                    x
                    and oxygen‐reduction‐associated suppression of spontaneous Cu release from Cu–N–C. These results highlight the importance of temporal fidelity for assigning transient dissolution chemistry at dynamic electrocatalyst interfaces.

title: Highly Adaptable Electrochemical Lithium Extraction From Brine via Heterojunction Engineering
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrochemical lithium extraction from salt‐lake brines has received extensive attention due to its low energy consumption, environmental friendliness, and high efficiency. However, conventional electrode materials suffer from sluggish desolvation kinetics and competing cations intercalation (Na
                    +
                    ) in the diverse brine environment across the world. Herein, a heterojunction engineering strategy was proposed to solve the above challenges. A lithium titanium oxides (LTO) heterojunction was rationally designed and constructed on the surface of LiFePO
                    4
                    (named LFP‐SEF), which could expedite the desolvation process of Li
                    +
                    via the induced built‐in electric field and suppress competing cation intercalation via size sieving. Consequently, the LFP‐SEF‐based device consistently delivers outstanding lithium extraction performance in a series of brines (Na/Li ≈ 1–150) around the world. Even in the brine from southern Tibet (Dangxiongcuo Salt Lake) with a high Na/Li mass ratio of 150, LFP‐SEF also exhibits 83.72% capacity retention after 50 cycles with high separation factor (Na/Li ≈ 989.80; Mg/Li ≈1856.50). The exceptional performance is preserved as the device size increases from lab‐scale to production‐scale (1.5 m
                    2
                    ), demonstrating its excellent industrialization prospects. The concept of heterojunction engineering proposed in this work opens a promising route to industrial‐scale lithium extraction in complex brine environment.

title: Magnetic Switching of Exciton Lifetime in CrSBr
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Exciton dynamics in layered magnetic semiconductors provide a sensitive probe of the interplay between spin order and light–matter interaction. Here, we study thin CrSBr layers using time‐resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy in an external magnetic field, revealing a step‐like reduction in the exciton lifetime from 11 to 7 ps during the magnetization flip from the antiferromagnetic to the ferromagnetic phase. The reduction of the exciton lifetime in the ferromagnetic phase persists below the Néel temperature, as evidenced by its strong magnetic‐field dependence that disappears in the paramagnetic phase. Ab initio calculations reveal a one‐dimensional nature of free excitons, accompanied by a pronounced change in the oscillator strength across the magnetic phase transition, predicting a shorter radiative lifetime of free excitons in the antiferromagnetic phase of CrSBr, contradicting the experimental observations. This discrepancy is explained by strong localization of excitons at low temperature. We show both experimentally and theoretically that the observed magnetic switching of the exciton lifetime is attributed to a larger exciton localization volume leading to a larger oscillator strength in the ferromagnetic phase. The results show that disorder‐induced localization effects play a key role in exciton dynamics in CrSBr.

title: Data‐Driven Conformational Mismatch Design Enables Extreme‐Temperature Energy Storage in Copolyimides
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐temperature capacitive energy storage requires polymer dielectrics to combine a wide optical bandgap (
                    E
                    g
                    ) with a high glass‐transition temperature (
                    
                      T
                      g
                    
                    ), properties that are often difficult to optimize simultaneously through conventional backbone design. Here, we introduce conformational mismatch into semi‐alicyclic polyimide copolymers and identify promising monomer combinations through a multistage workflow integrating machine‐learning prediction of
                    T
                    g
                    , density‐functional‐theory calculations of electronic structure, and molecular‐dynamics analysis of chain conformations. Incorporating a methyl‐substituted diamine yields Co‐PI‐tC, in which local conformational mismatch modifies molecular fluctuations and chain packing while suppressing thermally activated charge transport. Conformational entropy estimates derived from atomic fluctuations quantitatively capture these changes and complement conventional structural and electronic descriptors. The resulting Co‐PI‐tC film combines a
                    T
                    g
                    of 271.52°C with
                    E
                    g
                    of 4.28 eV, delivers a discharged energy density of 8.6 J cm
                    −3
                    at 200°C with 90% efficiency and retains 6.7 J cm
                    −3
                    at 250°C, setting a high‐temperature energy‐storage record among reported copolymer dielectrics. These results establish conformational mismatch as an effective molecular‐design strategy for reconciling thermal stability and electrical insulation in high‐temperature polymer dielectrics.

title: An Electrically Gated Solid‐State Thermal Transistor for Energy‐Efficient Thermal Management
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Vapor‐compression heating and cooling systems dominate modern thermal management, yet their efficiency and scalability remain constrained by mechanical complexity and refrigerant‐based operation. Solid‐state approaches offer an attractive alternative, with recent demonstrations showing the potential for highly efficient, compact thermal control. Here we demonstrate an electrically gated solid‐state thermal transistor based on bulk single‐crystal barium titanate, achieving a switching ratio of 1.6, among the highest reported for bulk ferroelectrics. We further introduce switching efficiency as a figure of merit, reaching ∼8.52 cm
                    3
                    J
                    −1
                    , more than two orders of magnitude higher than that of the highest‐performing reported thermal switch, PbZrO
                    3
                    . Unlike previous thermal switches that operate between two discrete states, this device provides continuously tunable thermal‐conductivity states, enabling transistor‐like modulation and amplification of heat flow. In situ x‐ray diffraction combined with first‐principles calculations shows that switching originates from anisotropic phonon transport between ferroelectric domains. Integrated into a proof‐of‐concept thermal‐management system, the device shifts the baseline temperature of a miniature human analog by ∼0.6°C at a cycle‐averaged power input of 33 µW cm
                    −2
                    , approximately ninefold lower than a vapor‐compression heat pump performing the same task. These results establish ferroelectric thermal transistors as a programmable, energy‐efficient platform for solid‐state thermal management.

title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca
                    2+
                    -ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca
                    2+
                    to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca
                    2+
                    cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution show that both compounds bind the same previously unrecognized activation hotspot in the transmembrane domain, a shallow groove formed by helices M3 and M4 and capped by M1. Despite limited chemical similarity, both activators share conserved interactions with Ser265 and Trp272 and stimulate Ca
                    2+
                    -dependent ATPase activity. Activator binding promotes a catalytically competent, calcium-bound E1-like conformation of SERCA that may involve altered protein-lipid interactions. These findings establish a structural framework for rational design of potent next-generation SERCA activators.

title: Breakdown of the classical rupture theory and earthquake propagation in the “forbidden” super-Rayleigh range
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Earthquakes propagating faster than the shear wave-speed are commonly thought to undergo a supershear transition upon which they discontinuously jump from the sub-Rayleigh regime to the supershear one. The super-Rayleigh regime, i.e., the range of propagation speeds between the Rayleigh and shear wave-speeds, is regarded as “forbidden” by the two-dimensional classical rupture theory. Here, we revisit the assumptions underlying the classical theory and develop a rupture theory that takes into account the dependence of the fault strength (frictional resistance) on the slip rate. The theory quantitatively agrees with numerical simulations nearly up to the Rayleigh wave-speed. Yet, very close to the latter, numerical rupture solutions change their character due to frictional rate nonlinearity, involving rate-strengthening friction, and rupture continuously propagates through the “forbidden” super-Rayleigh range into the supershear regime, without a sharp supershear transition. These results demonstrate that frictional rate dependence, generically observed in experiments, can have profound implications for fast earthquake propagation.

title: Multimodal robotic matter enabled by unified magnetic control primitives
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Robotic matter seeks to achieve collective functionality through interactions among modular units governed by global control signals. A persistent challenge is identifying control frameworks that are simultaneously scalable and deterministic. Here, we introduce a unified magnetic control paradigm that enables multimodal robotic matter using a minimal set of global-field primitives. We show that combinations of rotating and pulsed uniform fields, together with controlled field gradients, are sufficient to generate diverse behaviors—including multimodal locomotion, deterministic bottom-up assembly, and rapid, reversible shape morphing in origami-inspired modular robots. Each module incorporates permanent magnets with prescribed chirality and magnetic moment, encoding mechanical and magnetic asymmetries that map global field inputs to predictable forces, torques, and deformation pathways. Using a programmable three-dimensional Helmholtz coil system, we demonstrate four locomotion modes (rolling, steering, sliding, and walking), hierarchical assembly of three-dimensional robotic architectures, and millisecond-timescale transitions among discrete stable states, with applications to origami state machines and global shape change for navigation through confined spaces. By unifying locomotion, assembly, and reconfiguration within a single control framework, this work establishes a generalizable approach to magnetic robotic matter in which multifunctional collective behaviors emerge from a minimal set of control primitives.

title: TREX1 and TREX2 3′ → 5′ DNA exonucleases enhance the fidelity of translesion synthesis by DNA polymerase θ
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
A multiplicity of translesion synthesis (TLS) DNA polymerases (Pols) promote replication through DNA lesions in an error-free or error-prone manner. Among these Pols, Polθ operates in an error-prone manner. However, Polθ conducts TLS in human cells in a much more error-free manner than implicated from the high error-proneness of the purified Pol. To resolve this incongruity, here we show that the TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonucleases are integral components of TLS mediated by Polθ. In TREX1- or TREX2-deficient cells, Polθ-dependent TLS becomes nonoperational and chromosomal instability rises similar to that in Polθ-deficient cells. Consequently, similar to that in Polθ
                    −/−
                    mice,
                    
                      trex2
                      −/−
                    
                    mice exhibit increased susceptibility to ultraviolet-induced skin cancers. Furthermore, our findings that in the absence of TREX1/TREX2 3′ → 5′ exonuclease activities, Polθ-mediated TLS manifests high mutagenicity, and an increase in the diversity of misincorporated nucleotides demarcate a crucial role of these exonucleases in the removal of Polθ misinsertions and, thereby, in enhancing Polθ TLS fidelity and the consequent genome stability.

title: Resolving topological obstructions to vectorial structured field control
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The use of structured matter, such as optical retarders, for vectorial control is a well-established and widely used technique in modern optics, and has driven continued advances in the manipulation of complex, spatially varying vectorial fields. However, achieving arbitrary field conversion typically requires the use of cascaded elements, as intrinsic physical and fabrication constraints fundamentally limit individual devices to a restricted subset of transformations. This results in an overall continuous transformation potentially failing to be continuous at the level of the parameters of the cascade, leading to detrimental engineering consequences such as the introduction of complex, discontinuous aberrations that disrupt important topological properties of the underlying light and matter fields. In this work, we establish a mathematical framework for analyzing the topological difficulties that emerge in the decomposition of an overall transformation into individual layers, and for determining the minimal depth required to overcome them. The strategy introduced provides a general pathway for optimizing designs for vectorial field control and matter field generation, with particular importance for the manipulation of topological phases in optical polarization fields, such as Stokes skyrmions, where continuity is of vital importance.

title: Characterizing ocean flows with the scattering transform
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Upper-ocean flows are a complex multiscale jigsaw puzzle of turbulence and waves. Characterizing these flows is essential for understanding their role in redistributing heat, carbon, and nutrients. While power spectral analysis offers a useful statistical descriptor of these flows, it cannot always distinguish between different types of motion. We show that the scattering transform (ST), a wavelet convolution method, can extract geometric information from flow fields, offering insights beyond the power spectrum. The ST distinguishes balanced dynamics, internal waves, and different flavors of geophysical turbulence—even when their power spectra are identical. Applied to sea surface height (SSH) fields from ocean models, the ST differentiates regions with distinct underlying dynamics. Our analysis offers a framework for interpreting SSH from satellite altimetry and for analyzing other spatial maps (e.g., from airborne and coastal radar). More generally, the ST is an appealing way to characterize complex fluid motion in a variety of contexts.

title: Visual learning through auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Visual learning, like other kinds of learning, has classically been attributed to intensive, active training; however, whether it can be achieved via effortless, passive reactivation remains unresolved. Here, we triggered targeted reactivation using auditory tones that had acquired contextual meaning through preceding visual–auditory associative learning. Re-exposure to learned tones improved subsequent visual performance during both wakefulness and slow-wave sleep. Wake reactivation matched training in both improvement and improvement per trial, whereas sleep reactivation surpassed both wake reactivation and training. By contrast, re-exposure to unlearned tones impaired performance only during slow-wave sleep. Reactivation-induced improvement and impairment were strictly orientation- and location-specific and were associated with a convergent auditory–visual coupling pathway. Beyond this shared pathway, auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep unfolded through distinct coupling architectures linking sensory and higher-order cortical regions. Collectively, our findings establish auditory reactivation as a highly efficient route to visual learning, identify sleep as its most potent state, and reveal a double-edged, state-dependent neuroplastic architecture.

title: Errors in social network knowledge predict how ties evolve in the future
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
A notable feature of people’s social knowledge is that it is riddled with errors. These errors, e.g., making mistakes about who are actually friends in a social network, has typically been attributed to cognitive limitations or heuristics that prioritize knowledge of general social patterns over details about specific ties. Here, we demonstrate that such errors instead reflect an adaptive link prediction process that anticipates how the network will evolve far into the future. By longitudinally following a large, real-world social network (
                    n
                     = 196) and tracking the formation and dissolution of social ties over the course of a year, we show that judgments that are wrong in the moment accurately forecast which relationships will emerge or dissolve up to 6 months later. On average, participants’ errors predicted tie formation nearly 3× and tie loss more than 1.2× above chance levels. Beyond the use of simple heuristics like triadic closure and homophily, computational modeling reveals that successful link prediction relies on mental representations of the social network that integrates information about both direct and indirect, long-range ties between individuals. Having a social network representation that is future-oriented yields distinct social advantages: Those who are better able to predict changes in the network become more centrally positioned over time, contingent on their initial position.

title: Oligodendrocyte ER-phagy restricts excessive myelination by degrading sphingolipid synthases
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Myelination is critical for nervous system function. Numerous signaling pathways have been identified that promote myelin sheath growth, disruption of which can lead to hypomyelination. However, the negative regulators of myelin sheath expansion remain poorly defined. Here, we identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–phagy as a cellular brake on central nervous system myelination that restricts myelin sheath thickness during brain development. ER-phagy is active in oligodendrocytes during myelin membrane expansion and limits the abundance of ER-resident sphingolipid synthases, including ceramide synthase 2 (Cers2). Impairment of ER-phagy accumulates ER, elevates sphingolipid production, drives excessive myelin thickening, and alters social behavior after prolonged juvenile social isolation. Genetic deletion of Cers2, which synthesizes long-chain ceramides essential for sphingolipid biogenesis, rescues the hypermyelination phenotype caused by ER-phagy disruption. Together, our findings establish that ER-phagy–sphingolipid axis represses myelin growth and reveal a mechanistic link between ER homeostasis and myelin production by oligodendrocytes, providing insight into the cellular mechanisms underlying pathological hypermyelination.

title: Strategic coexistence theory for evolutionary games
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Evolutionary game theory and ecological coexistence theory both seek to predict the outcome of competition between biological entities, be they strategies or species, but the two fields have relied on largely separate approaches. Replicator equations provide a foundation for predicting the outcome of strategic competition, but comparing how different mechanisms alter competition across games remains challenging. Inspired by modern coexistence theory from community ecology, we develop Strategic Coexistence Theory (SCT), which translates payoff-based invasion conditions at monomorphic boundary conditions into strategic niche differences and fitness differences between any two competing strategies described by classic replicator dynamics. We show that SCT recovers the classic classification of two-strategy games and also allows us to compare mechanisms for the evolution of cooperation within a shared niche-fitness difference space. In stochastic games, environmental stochasticity increases both boundary invasion growth rates, whereas in multiplayer public-goods games, nonlinear benefits can either stabilize or destabilize competition. These applications also show that the number or stability of internal equilibria generally cannot be predicted from invasion growth rates at monomorphic boundaries, illustrating a key limitation of characterizing competitive systems using boundary invasion rates alone. Together, these results show that SCT provides a coexistence-theoretic perspective for characterizing how different mechanisms alter strategy competition across games.

title: Design of ionic self-assembled monolayers suppressing proton release to mitigate proton-based degradation of perovskite solar cells
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) serve as effective hole-transport layers (HTLs) in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), facilitating energy-level alignment and defect passivation at perovskite interfaces. However, their integration is limited by weak anchoring to transparent conducting oxides (TCOs), resulting in desorption during deposition and the release of acidic protons, which react with components of the perovskite leading to degradation [T. To strengthen anchoring between the SAM and TCO while simultaneously mitigating proton-induced degradation of the perovskite, we have prepared ionic SAMs featuring a phosphonate anchoring group and a perovskite-compatible cation.                     [Me-4PACz]
                    −
                    as the HTL in lead-based PSCs results in devices with a PCE of 26.53%, outperforming the PCE of 24.97% for the Me-4PACz-based device. After heating at 85°C for over 1,000 h, the [FA]
                    +
                    [Me-4PACz]
                    −
                    -based device retained ca. 88% of its initial efficiency. This study establishes the broad utility of ionic SAMs as versatile compounds to concurrently increase device efficiency and long-term stability.

title: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; genus
                    Orthopneumovirus
                    ) causes severe pneumonia in young children worldwide, yet the zoonotic potential of the few known nonhuman animal orthopneumoviruses remains unknown. Here, we characterized a highly divergent bat orthopneumovirus (BPV) from West African straw-colored fruit bats and established a systematic framework for evaluating zoonotic risk posed by an emerging viral pathogen. Epidemiologic data in bats showed a low viral detection rate (24 of 1778 RT-PCR positive) and low seroprevalence (6 of 66 IgG IFA positive), suggesting BPV episodic circulation potentially sustained in immunologically naïve bats following bat birthing events. Near-complete genomes from two BPV genetic variants revealed prototypic orthopneumovirus organization, but lacked the
                    SH
                    viroporin-encoding gene present in RSV. Functional experiments showed that BPV NS1/NS2 antagonized human interferon β responses, and that BPV pseudoviruses entered human cells (4.5- to 53.5-fold less efficiently than RSV), while being cross-neutralized by human RSV-reactive antisera, together suggesting zoonotic traits that may be partly constrained by cross-protective immunity. BPV escaped neutralization by RSV-specific therapeutic palivizumab and inhibition by lonafarnib, but remained susceptible to MPE8, a broad-spectrum monoclonal antibody that targets the conserved pneumovirus antigenic site III. These findings identify zoonotic traits of a divergent bat pneumovirus while suggesting potential protective value of preexisting RSV immunity and broad-spectrum interventions, which has implications for pandemic preparedness. Whether cross-protection in the human population may change by the advent of RSV vaccination warrants investigation. Efforts to investigate orthopneumovirus host shifts, reservoir studies, and development of broadly reactive orthopneumovirus vaccines and antivirals are warranted.

title: Modulating chain conformations and hydrogen-bond dynamics at silica–rubber interfaces for enhanced energy dissipation in composites
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The polymer–nanoparticle interphase is essential for fabricating high-performance nanocomposites, as it dictates mechanical properties through interfacial stress transfer and energy dissipation. However, engineering the buried interphases remains challenging due to the complex hierarchical structure and methodological limitations, particularly in silica–rubber systems where confined polymer chain conformation and hydrogen-bond dynamics are poorly resolved. Herein, a selective polymer-removal technique was developed to strip free and loosely bound polymer under extreme conditions, enabling TEM visualization of polymer chain-like interfacial features consistent with train-, loop-, and tail-like adsorption motifs in silica/silicone rubber nanocomposites. Correlative analysis combining STEM-EELS, high-resolution NMR, in situ variable-temperature IR, and 2D low-field NMR spectroscopy resolves hydrogen bonding between silica surface hydroxyls and silicone backbone oxygen atoms (Si-O-H···O-Si), which exhibit temperature-dependent behavior. Quantitative analysis reveals the strategic modulation of interphase layer thickness: As the apparent hydroxyl density of silica varied from 2.1 to 12.9 OH nm
                    −2
                    , the interphase thickness increased from 4.1 ± 0.8 nm to 13.2 ± 1.4 nm (9.5 mol% polymer phenyl); increasing the polymer phenyl content to 29.7 mol% further expands the layer to 23.4 ± 1.0 nm. Molecular dynamics simulations also suggest that higher silica surface hydroxyl density enhances multipoint adsorption of polymer chain, which promotes the formation of loop and train conformations. These confined chain arrangements are consistent with the reduced Arrhenius activation energy from 101 to 50 kJ mol
                    −1
                    measured by dynamic rheology, which facilitates interfacial chain mobility and hydrogen-bond exchange during deformation. These findings provide molecular-level insights for the rational design of polymer nanocomposites.

title: Mechanical instability generates monodisperse colloidosomes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Formation and rupture of vesicles are fundamental processes underlying diverse phenomena in biology, materials science, and biomedical applications. Vesicles form when the area of a growing disk-like membrane reaches the instability point at which the energy barrier to the disk-to-vesicle transition vanishes. Observing such topological transitions in lipid bilayers is a challenge because of their nanoscale dimensions and rapid dynamics. We study a scaled-up model of membranes assembled from rod-shaped colloidal particles. The unique features of colloidal membranes enable the real-time visualization of spontaneous vesicle closure driven by an instability arising from competition between edge and bending energies that is universal to all membrane-based materials. A continuum theory with independently measured material parameters quantitatively predicts the instability point for vesicle formation and intermediate membrane conformations during the disk-to-vesicle transition. The instability generates monodisperse, selectively permeable colloidosomes whose size is controlled by gravity and membrane elasticity, providing a scalable and programmable platform for diverse applications.

title: A sweeping twist defect as a topological flagellum that enhances colloid translation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Nematic liquid crystals can dramatically reconfigure under dynamic forcing, providing exciting opportunities in active matter. Here, we study a disk colloid with hybrid planar and homeotropic anchoring rotated by an external magnetic field which generates a dynamic companion topological defect. The disk moves faster when the defect sweeps across the disk’s face. We identify the defect as a nonsingular twist wall, characterize the twist energy landscape, and identify that the sweeping motion is driven by a topological instability. As the defect sweeps, it reverses the handedness of twist and lowers the free energy in the fluid in the gap above the disk. Landau–de Gennes modeling shows that the sweeping wall behaves as a propagating director texture: the director field is nearly stationary in the wall frame, while nematogens rotate locally as the wall passes. The nematogens’ rotation generates a viscous stress on the surface of the disk that hastens its propulsion. Thus, the defect acts as a flagellum that powers colloid swimming, providing an example of a dissipative topological structure whose dynamics can be harnessed to perform useful work.

title: Age-associated B cells drive lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder in Faslpr mice through the p38α−CXCL10 signaling axis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Defective Fas cell surface death receptor (FAS) signaling leads to lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder, yet the mechanisms involved remain unclear. Using genetic mouse models homozygous for the lymphoproliferation spontaneous mutation (
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    ), we showed that age-associated B cells (ABCs) were critical drivers of lymphadenopathy and autoimmunity. Single-cell transcriptomics of lymph node immune cells in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice revealed a marked expansion of ABCs. Depletion of these ABCs in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice significantly restrained lymph node enlargement and alleviated autoimmune manifestations, whereas adoptive transfer of ABCs from
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice to wild-type mice exacerbated disease pathology. Mechanistically, p38α signaling emerged as a critical regulator of ABC differentiation and function, and conditional deletion of p38α in CD11c
                    +
                    cells profoundly suppressed ABC expansion and ameliorated autoimmune manifestations in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice. Furthermore, we identified CXCL10 as an important downstream effector of p38α signaling in ABCs that drives autoimmune disorder. Neutralization of CXCL10 significantly attenuated disease severity in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice. Although clinical relevance analyses of autoimmune patient cohorts revealed a parallel expansion of ABCs in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and primary Sjögren’s syndrome, ABCs with higher p38α content were specifically enriched in SLE patients. Together, these findings identify p38α-driven ABCs as an important regulator of lymphoproliferative and autoimmune disorder in
                    
                      Fas
                      lpr
                    
                    mice and suggest that targeting the p38α−CXCL10 axis in ABCs may be a therapeutic strategy for treating this autoimmune disease.
