title: Pinning of Van Hove singularities and correlated insulators in M-valley twisted transition metal dichalcogenides
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We investigate the role of long-range Coulomb interactions in M-valley moirés using the self-consistent Hartree–Fock approximation. This platform was recently proposed [D. Călugăru et al.,
                    Nature
                    643
                    , 376–381 (2025) and C. Lei
                    et al., Phys. Rev. Lett.
                    135
                    , 196402 (2025)] as a new class of experimentally realizable moiré materials using twisted transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) homobilayers with the 1T structure. While these seminal studies considered the noninteracting theory without an electric displacement field, this work shows that both electron–electron interactions at finite doping and an interlayer bias strongly modify the moiré bands. For small twists (
                    
                      
                        ≲
                      
                    
                    5°) the density of states versus filling and interlayer bias displays qualitatively different behavior for twisting near aligned (0°) and antialigned (60°) stacking with tunable Van Hove singularities (VHSs). Moreover, interactions pin the VHS to the Fermi energy over a finite range of doping both at zero and finite bias depending on the stacking type, an effect known to enhance both superconductivity and strongly correlated states. At half-filling, we obtain the phase diagram as a function of interaction strength, interlayer bias, and twist angle. We find a competition driven by band mixing between an isotropic ferromagnet and an antiferromagnet that are nearly degenerate over a wide range of experimentally accessible parameters. Our work demonstrates that correlated states in M-valley twisted TMD homobilayers can be strongly tuned in situ both by applying an electric displacement field and by electron doping.

title: A nanoscale gap junction–perinexus nanodomain governs balance of ephaptic and gap-junctional activation in excitable cell pairs
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Electrical communication between excitable cells depends on gap junction (GJ) currents and field-mediated ephaptic interactions, but their relative contributions have been difficult to quantify, limiting insight into arrhythmia and other disorders of bioelectric signaling. Building on the nanoscale, sodium channel-rich perinexus at the cardiac intercalated disc, we developed a “Single-on-Paired” (SoP) preparation, recording whole-cell sodium current from one adult ventricular myocyte that remains coupled by an intercalated disc to an intact partner. This revealed a composite two-cell sodium current with two rising-phase slopes and an activation jump between closely spaced voltage steps, an “Intercalated Disc Signature” (IDS) absent from isolated single myocytes and providing a direct readout of intercellular activation. Rapid sodium channel activation cannot be resolved under voltage clamp at physiological extracellular sodium ([Na
                    +
                    ]
                    o
                    ), so SoP recordings used reduced [Na
                    +
                    ]
                    o
                    of 25 to 35 mM. Within this nonphysiologic range, graded GJ inhibition, perinexal widening with an Scn1b-derived competitive adhesion peptide, and [Na
                    +
                    ]
                    o
                    modulation showed that GJ inhibition abolished the IDS at 25 mM, whereas a modest 10 mM rise to 35 mM restored it despite persistent GJ inhibition. GJ coupling and a perinexus-centered ephaptic mechanism are thus separable contributors to intercellular activation whose relative engagement is set by extracellular sodium. A two-cell computational model constrained by these data reproduces the IDS and predicts that at physiological 145 mM [Na
                    +
                    ]
                    o
                    with reduced GJ conductance, perinexus-centered ephaptic mechanisms suffice for intercellular activation. Clamping cleft potential, but not cleft sodium, disrupts this behavior in silico, identifying cleft potential as the proximal ephaptic signal.

title: A deep-learning-boosted framework for quantum sensing with nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a versatile quantum sensing platform for high sensitivity measurements of magnetic fields, temperature, and strain with nanoscale spatial resolution. A common bottleneck is the analysis of optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra, where target quantities are encoded in resonance features. Conventional nonlinear fitting is often computationally expensive, sensitive to initialization, and prone to failure at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Here we introduce a robust, efficient machine learning (ML) framework for real-time ODMR analysis based on a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN). The model performs direct parameter inference without initial guesses or iterative optimization, and is naturally parallelizable on graphics processing units (GPU) for high-throughput processing. We validate the approach on both synthetic and experimental datasets, showing improved throughput, accuracy, and robustness than standard nonlinear fitting, with the largest gains in the low-SNR regime. We further validate our methods in two representative sensing applications: diagnosing intracellular temperature changes using nanodiamond probes and widefield magnetic imaging of superconducting vortices in a high-temperature superconductor. This deep-learning inference framework enables fast and reliable extraction of physical parameters from complex ODMR data and provides a scalable route to real-time quantum sensing and imaging.

title: The Yersinia pestis effector YopM binds the human pyrin death domain to inhibit inflammasome activation and effector-triggered immunity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Bacteria in the genus
                    Yersinia
                    use type III secretion to inject several effectors into phagocytes to disrupt signaling. Two effectors disrupt host signaling by inactivation of RhoA, triggering pyrin inflammasome assembly in infected phagocytes and protective immunity. A third protein, YopM, counteracts effector-triggered immunity by binding to and inactivating pyrin. Prior evidence suggested that gain of function codon changes in the pyrin gene
                    MEFV
                    that cause Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) and provide resistance to
                    Yersinia pestis
                    were selected to evade YopM binding. YopM was shown to bind an N-terminal region of human pyrin, which includes the eponymous pyrin domain (PYD), however, the interaction mechanism was undefined. Using bacterial two-hybrid assay, protein biochemistry, and X-ray crystallography, we determined that YopM binds to the PYD, which has few validated FMF amino acid variants. We show that YopM binds PYD R42, a “Site 2” amino acid important for positive and negative regulation of pyrin and that binding to the R42W variant is reduced. YopM amino acid change variants defective for PYD binding failed to inhibit the pyrin inflammasome in human monocytes infected with
                    Yersinia
                    . In addition, PYD binding was dispensable for YopM to inhibit the inflammasome in murine macrophages, suggesting this effector uses a distinct mechanism to target mouse pyrin. These results define that
                    Y. pestis
                    YopM binds to human PYD to promote pathogenesis, and because Site 2 variants that evade YopM binding have low gain of function inflammasome activity, these data may explain why most validated FMF codon changes are in other domains of pyrin.

title: A two-dimensional molecular gearbox operated in a crystalline solid
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Since the earliest artificial gears, parallel gearbox systems based on intermeshing two-dimensional (2D) networks of multiple gear units have served a fundamental role in macroscale mechanical devices through the correlated mechanical motion of multiple gears. However, the realization of molecular-level 2D gearbox machinery with correlated motion among multiple units remains highly challenging. Here, we report a molecular-level 2D gearbox in a crystal, formed through the supramolecular assembly of an Au(I)-complex rotor with tripodal triptycene and triadamantyl phosphine (Ad
                    3
                    P) rotators, connected via an ethynyl–Au(I) unit. Upon heating, the rotators within a 2D hexagonal gear network exhibit 120° site-exchange rotational motion in a correlated manner, as revealed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD),
                    2
                    H solid-state (SS) NMR spectroscopy, and time-resolved variable-temperature XRD measurements. In addition, density functional theory calculations provide insight into the energetic preference for correlated motion within the gear-network. This 2D intermolecular gearbox in the crystalline state represents a supramolecular platform in which the intermolecular gearing motion has a large impact on the bulk crystal, which could provide a bridge between molecular-level mechanical properties and macroscale SS physical functions.

title: Compound heterozygosity for I692del and V726A variants in MEFV leads to severe autoinflammation and elevated interleukin-18 (CHIVE-18)
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We describe a severe
                    MEFV
                    -associated autoinflammatory disease, distinct from familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), and designate it CHIVE-18 syndrome (Compound Heterozygosity for I692del and V726A
                    MEFV
                    variants and Elevated IL-18). We present the clinical features and inflammatory signatures of 44 CHIVE-18 patients and 9 other patients with two
                    MEFV
                    variants including I692del. Clinical findings in CHIVE-18 patients often include transfusion-dependent anemia, arthritis, organomegaly, inflammatory bowel disease, failure to thrive, and less frequently cytokine storm, Amyloid A (AA) amyloidosis, and neutrophilic dermatoses. Serum total and free IL-18 levels in CHIVE-18 patients were markedly elevated compared to those of healthy controls, classical FMF patients, and compound heterozygotes for I692del and a pathogenic
                    MEFV
                    variant other than V726A and were comparable to the previously described levels of patients with pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne syndrome. Cultured U937 cells expressing the V726A/I692del double mutant exhibited significantly increased release of IL-1β, IL-18, and lactate dehydrogenase compared to the other FMF-associated mutants. Patients’ myeloid cells showed enhanced STAT1 phosphorylation after stimulation with IFNγ. Despite having undetectable serum IL-1β, a previously reported CHIVE-18 patient with autoimmune hepatitis had in situ staining of a liver biopsy that showed high expression of IL-1β, TNFα, and IL-18, which localized to CD68+ tissue macrophages. CHIVE-18 patients usually require an IL-1 inhibitor and sometimes combination therapy with another biologic to control disease activity. In summary, CHIVE-18 is a distinct, severe disease that expands the spectrum of
                    MEFV
                    -associated autoinflammatory disorders and highlights genotype/phenotype complexity in compound heterozygous disorders.

title: Unlocking the unparalleled paleoclimate record of Antarctic blue ice areas
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Ice uniquely provides direct samples of ancient atmosphere, enabling measurements of greenhouse gases contemporaneous to temperature reconstructions. Blue ice areas (covering 1% of the surface of Antarctica) hold a largely underexplored paleoclimate record that can extend beyond deep ice cores (that is, older than 1.5 My), covering periods in which global surface temperatures were similar to projected future temperatures. Blue ice areas expose ancient ice directly at the surface or at shallow depths due to net ablation and redirected ice flow, providing access to old ice at logistically reduced costs. However, the analysis and interpretation of blue ice samples is challenging, given the complex flow patterns in these regions that result in tilted layers, inversions and discontinuities in the stratigraphy, and complex ice–bedrock interactions. This paper presents a succinct review of state-of-the-art blue ice research, placed in the context of established ice core research, and argues that to advance the search for ancient ice, efforts in blue ice areas should focus on: i) collecting dated surface samples, ii) investigating the relationship between the age of the ice and other datable evidence, such as moraines, dust layers, meteorites, and exposed bedrock, and iii) developing models that can capture the typically disturbed or discontinuous stratigraphy. Together with advances in analytical techniques that address, for example, contamination and absolute dating, these efforts could lead to the recovery of the oldest ice on Earth, unravel warm climates of the past, and improve future climate change projections.

title: Temperature-dependent kinetic isotope effects in methane reactions with OH and Cl reshape atmospheric sink fractionation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The abundances of stable isotopes in methane (CH
                    4
                    ) are used to distinguish fossil and biological emissions and to constrain the global methane budget. While these analyses require correction for isotopic fractionation occurring in methane’s atmospheric reactions, the temperature dependence of the kinetic isotope effects (KIEs) are poorly described and typically ignored. Here we combine density functional theory, Møller–Plesset perturbation theory, coupled-cluster calculations, and tunneling-corrected transition state theory to develop a first-principles description of the temperature-dependent KIEs for CH
                    4
                    and its isotopologues reacting with OH and Cl over the range 100 to 500 K which exhibit substantial and previously neglected temperature dependence. Incorporation of these KIEs into the EMAC chemistry–climate model yields systematically different effective atmospheric sink fractionation factors than those obtained using temperature-invariant values. The largest differences occur for chlorine oxidation in the cold upper troposphere and stratosphere, where methane isotope budgets are particularly sensitive to reactive halogens. We find a weak
                    13
                    C–D clumping anomaly and a strong D–D clumping anomaly, confirming earlier work and demonstrating that atmospheric oxidation produces substantial enrichment in Δ
                    12
                    CH
                    2
                    D
                    2
                    , and helping to reconcile source signatures with atmospheric observations. These results show that temperature-dependent KIEs are required for robust interpretation of methane isotopes in both contemporary and past atmospheres.

title: Contrasting spatial homogeneity in atmospheric ice-nucleating particles from local to synoptic scales
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Ice-nucleating particles (INPs) play a critical role in regulating glaciation and precipitation formation in mixed-phase cloud (containing liquid and ice), yet their spatial variability across different scales remains poorly constrained. In this study, coordinated immersion freezing INP measurements from multiple sites during two campaigns in an urban–rural environment and complex mountainous terrain were used to investigate INP spatial distributions at tens-of-kilometer scales. At these scales, INP concentrations were generally spatially homogeneous during each campaign, indicating that single-site measurements can often represent surrounding areas. Occasional spatial differences were observed at warm activation temperatures (higher than −20 °C), ascribed to variations in heat-labile, likely biological INPs. Extending the analysis to the synoptic scale across multiple campaigns, warm-temperature INPs showed greater site-to-site differences, suggesting stronger influences from local or regional sources. In contrast, INPs active at colder temperatures showed much stronger spatial similarity between two inland continental sites separated by 800 km, revealing a broader regional coherence in this INP population. This was also observed at the coastal site, but only under continental air mass influence; the similarity weakened under marine air masses. These results suggest that cold-temperature INPs may reflect a broader INP background over continents such as that contributed by windblown dust. Our findings provide direct observational constraints on the representativeness of single-site INP measurements, which can help inform the strategy for representing variations in INP populations in atmospheric models.

title: The circSRSF5-FUS-EIF4A3 regulatory circuitry protects Ewing sarcoma cells from EWS::FLI1 small-molecule inhibition
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have become a key focus in cancer research due to their high stability, diversity, and ability to regulate various biological processes. This study explores the impact of small-molecule inhibition of EWS::FLI1 oncogene by YK-4-279 in Ewing sarcoma (ES). ES is a rare and highly aggressive childhood cancer driven by fusion proteins that disrupt normal gene regulation and promote tumor growth. Current treatments rely on intensive chemotherapy with serious long-term side effects, emphasizing the need for targeted therapies. A promising new approach targets the interaction between EWS::FLI1 and the RNA helicase DHX9 through the small molecule YK-4-279, which displays strong antitumor effects and has advanced to clinical trials. Transcriptome profiling revealed widespread changes in circRNA expression after YK-4-279 treatment, with a notable up-regulation of
                    circSRSF5
                    . Functional and mechanistic evidence identifies a key role for
                    circSRSF5
                    in tumor cell survival by stabilizing the anti-apoptotic protein eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) and contributing to therapy resistance. These findings uncover a previously unidentified role for circRNAs, particularly
                    circSRSF5
                    , in ES pathogenesis and treatment response.

title: Hardware-encoded modality separation for multimodal sensing and artificial perception
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Human skin achieves robust perception by distributing modality-specialized receptors that preferentially encode mechanical and thermal cues. Yet, soft and flexible tactile sensors often suffer from cross-sensitivity, where stretching, bending, and temperature variations generate overlapping electrical readouts that undermine reliable multimodal measurement and downstream artificial intelligence–based interpretation. Here, we present a multimodal piezoresistive platform based on doped silicon nanomembranes that leverages their crystallographic anisotropy and a bilayer differential architecture for front-end modality separation. By integrating [110] longitudinal/transverse gauges with [100] reference gauges that exhibit reduced piezoresistive sensitivity but comparable temperature coefficient of resistance, together with a bilayer differential layout, the platform compensates thermal drift and decouples stretching from bending at the hardware level. Experimental and theoretical analyses establish a quantitative framework for separating modality-specific responses under combined stretching, bending, and temperature stimuli. Integrated into a flexible, wireless platform, the decoupled signals enable real-time transmission and deep learning–based interpretation, allowing accurate identification of geometrically similar objects with distinct thermal or mechanical properties. These results highlight the feasibility and need to co-design front-end sensing architectures and learning models to achieve robust, high-accuracy multimodal decoupling in real-world conditions.

title: Hybrid transverse thermoelectric conversion based on off-diagonal Peltier and Ettingshausen effects in a junction-less single material
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Transverse thermoelectric conversion, which interconverts heat and charge currents in orthogonal directions, is gaining attention as a driving principle for next-generation thermal management devices that do not require dissimilar material junctions or complex module structures. Transverse thermoelectric conversion is driven by various principles stemming from the breaking of structural symmetry or time-reversal symmetry, and substantial performance improvements are anticipated by simultaneously utilizing multiple principles. This study demonstrates hybrid transverse thermoelectric conversion based on multiple phenomena within a junction-less single material. Using an active thermoelectric imaging technique based on lock-in thermography, the charge-to-heat current conversion characteristics in Mg
                    3
                    Bi
                    2
                    crystals showing anisotropic transport properties were visualized and evaluated. We successfully separated the contributions of the off-diagonal Peltier effect due to the electronic structural symmetry breaking and the ordinary Ettingshausen effect due to the time-reversal symmetry breaking under a magnetic field. These contributions operate additively within the same material, leading to the notable enhancement of the transverse thermoelectric conversion performance.

title: Rapid intensification of summer convective precipitation in New England
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Anthropogenic warming is intensifying precipitation extremes, yet how subdaily convective rainfall responds in historically stratiform-dominated midlatitude regions remains poorly constrained. Using four decades of hourly station observations and reanalysis data, we show that summer convective precipitation has intensified across much of New England and surrounding regions from 1980 to 2020, with high-intensity events increasing in higher latitudes. Extreme convective rainfall scales at ∼13 to 14% per degree Celsius, nearly twice the Clausius-Clapeyron rate and significantly faster than stratiform precipitation. This intensification is accompanied by shorter event durations, increased moisture convergence, enhanced convective instability, and reduced antecedent soil moisture. Our results indicate a warming-driven shift toward convective dominance linked to changes in midlatitude circulation, reduced meridional temperature gradient, and land-atmosphere coupling, placing New England within an emerging poleward extension of the summer convective regime.

title: Surface-passivated high-entropy oxide-derived catalysts for stable dry reforming of methane
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Dry reforming of methane (DRM) enables the co-valorization of CO
                    2
                    and CH
                    4
                    into syngas, yet the development of sintering- and coking-resistant catalysts that suppress CH
                    4
                    cracking while accelerating coke gasification without compromising reaction efficiency remains a major challenge. Here, we address this challenge by employing surface-passivated catalysts derived from high-entropy oxides (HEOs) for stable DRM operation. Alkaline earth metal cation (M
                    2+
                    )-doped HEOs were designed to function without pretreatment and exhibited resistance to sintering and coking. This robustness arises from the in situ exsolution of NiCuCo alloy nanoparticles encapsulated within a multifunctional BaCO
                    3
                    overlayer, enabled by HEO-stabilized Ba incorporation and Ba-mediated surface reconstruction during DRM. This adaptive architecture passivates deep CH
                    4
                    cracking, promotes CO
                    2
                    activation, accelerates coke gasification, and thereby sustains catalytic efficiency and durability. Comprehensive spectroscopic, microscopic, and diffraction analyses revealed the structural dynamics and mechanistic pathways governing catalyst evolution under DRM conditions.

title: How far are we from a critical salinity in the North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre?
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The North Atlantic Subpolar Gyre (SPG) can undergo abrupt cooling associated with a loss of deep convection, yet the hydrographic conditions that drive this transition remain uncertain. While some CMIP6 models simulate an abrupt SPG cooling, others do not. Here, we identify a critical sea surface salinity (SSS) that separates these contrasting behaviors. Models without abrupt cooling either remain above this threshold because they project weak freshening or already lie below it under present-day conditions, inconsistent with observations. Observed SSS exceeds the critical threshold by 0.3 to 0.8 g kg
                    −1
                    , depending on the exact threshold definition. Although no declining trend is currently detected, observations remain consistent with models that simulate abrupt cooling. In these models, SSS begins to decline rapidly and crosses the critical threshold about 20 years after the onset of freshening. These results highlight the importance of sustained salinity observations for detecting the approach to this critical threshold, providing a physically based early warning of an abrupt SPG cooling.

title: Ultra-generalized hologram synthesis via domain-adaptive wavefront learning
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Deep learning–based computer-generated holography is essential for creating lifelike three-dimensional (3D) visuals in extended reality and immersive human-digital interaction. However, current data-driven approaches predominantly rely on a 3D-solution search strategy that couples scene representation with physical parameters. This paradigm leads to physical overfitting, restricting models to fixed wavelengths and depths and preventing generalization across diverse 3D data formats. Here, we report a 2D-solution search technique, wavefront-aware neural encoding (WNE). This method is a universal framework that overcomes these limitations via domain-adaptive wavefront learning. By compensating for feature distribution shifts induced by varying data formats and physical parameters, WNE maps various wavefronts into a unified feature domain compatible with a frozen, pretrained encoder. This mechanism enables ultra-generalized hologram synthesis: A single pretrained network can encode high-fidelity phase-only holograms for diverse 3D representations, from conventional layer-based data to emerging Gaussian splatting. Outperforming previous analytical and neural encoding methods in image quality, WNE establishes a robust, plug-and-play engine for diverse holographic applications.

title: Multimodal motion and behavior switching of multistable ciliary walkers
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The collective motion of arrays of cilia—tiny, hairlike protrusions—drives the locomotion of numerous microorganisms, enabling multimodal motion and switching between gaits to navigate complex environments. Inspired by this multimodal motion, we introduce multistable soft walkers with millimeter-scale flexible cilia that buckle under the walkers weight, coupling multistability and actuation within a single physical mechanism. When placed on a vibrating surface, the propulsion direction of ciliary walkers is selected through the buckled states of their cilia, allowing multimodal motion and switching between modes in response to perturbations. We first show that bimodal walkers with left-right symmetric cilia can reverse direction upon encountering obstacles. Next, we demonstrate that walkers with isotropic cilia exhibit both translational and rotational motion and switch between them in response to environmental interactions. At increasing densities, swarms of such walkers collectively transition from predominantly spinning to translational motion. Last, we show that the shape, placement, and number of cilia controls the modes of motion of the walkers. Our results establish a rational, physically grounded strategy for designing minimalist soft robots where complex behaviors emerge from feedback between internal mechanical states and environmental interactions, laying the foundation for soft robotic collectives that operate without onboard sensing or centralized control.

title: Umbilical cord structure shapes feto-maternal heat transfer across mammals
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The umbilical cord varies widely across placental mammals, yet the functional consequences of this structural diversity remain unclear. We compared cord anatomy across 130 mammal species, reconstructed ancestral states, and combined multimodal imaging with physics-based modeling of oxygen and heat transfer. Reconstructions indicate that the ancestral umbilical cord was uncoiled, with three vessels and an allantoic duct; the human combination of coiling with loss of the duct is rare. Across species, vessel number, duct persistence, and cord length increase with birth weight. Modeling predicts that oxygen delivery remains near maximal across architectures but that placental heat loss depends more strongly on umbilical flow and on cord length and coiling, suggesting more efficient cooling in larger mammals. Microscopy and ultrasound imaging reveal geometric vessel layouts, including a human triple helix, consistent with configurations predicted to reduce intervessel heat shunting. As fetuses must dissipate heat through the mother, these results link cord morphology, evolution, and fetal thermal resilience.

title: Skeletal muscle proteomics reveals metabolic phenotype–specific adaptations to exercise training in health, obesity, and type 2 diabetes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Exercise training improves metabolic health, including whole-body insulin sensitivity, yet the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We applied proteomics and phosphoproteomics to skeletal muscle biopsies from lean men, and men with obesity or type 2 diabetes (T2D), obtained before and after 8 weeks of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) under basal and insulin-stimulated conditions. Before HIIT, protein expression showed a stepwise progression from lean to obesity to T2D. HIIT induced more pronounced proteomic remodeling in obesity and T2D compared with lean men, characterized by increased mitochondrial and decreased proteasomal contents. Phosphoproteomic responses were diagnosis dependent, revealing distinct insulin signaling adaptations. Mechanistically, AMP-activated protein kinase γ2 (AMPKγ2) emerged as a prominent HIIT-regulated protein, exhibiting increased incorporation into AMPKα2β2 complexes across all phenotypes, and AMPKγ2 overexpression in human myotubes increased basal glucose oxidation. These findings elucidate molecular pathways underlying exercise-induced insulin sensitization and suggest AMPKγ2 as a candidate regulator for exercise-induced metabolic adaptation.

title: Continuously aligned biomimetic sites in MXene membranes for rapid lithium extraction
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Efficient separation of lithium ions (Li
                    +
                    ) from magnesium ions (Mg
                    2+
                    ) remains a central challenge for direct lithium extraction from salt lake brines due to their similar physicochemical properties. Inspired by biological ion channels, biomimetic membranes have been explored to improve Li
                    +
                    /Mg
                    2+
                    separation. However, most biomimetic membranes focus primarily on introducing recognition sites while overlooking the structural features of biological channels, particularly the continuous arrangement of coordination sites that facilitates efficient ion transport. Here, inspired by the continuous carbonyl coordination structure of the KcsA ion channel, 4-formylbenzo-15-crown-5 ether was periodically grafted onto poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) chains and integrated with MXene nanosheets to construct two-dimensional interlayer channels with continuously aligned crown ether recognition sites. This architecture shifts Li
                    +
                    transport from random diffusion to successive site-to-site hopping, reducing the effective transport energy barrier. The resulting biomimetic MXene membrane achieves a Li
                    +
                    flux of 0.12 mol·m
                    −2
                    ·h
                    −1
                    with Li
                    +
                    /Mg
                    2+
                    selectivity of 109 and performs effectively across various salt lake brines.

title: Stress unmasks disconnected endocrine coordination of glucose metabolism in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Skeletal muscle orchestrates systemic metabolism, dynamically coordinating glucose uptake and fuel use to match energy demand. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), loss of dystrophin is associated with altered metabolic regulation. Using physiological stress to unmask metabolic deficits in the
                    mdx
                    mouse model of DMD, we show that stress hormone signaling rises without an appropriate poststress rise in insulin secretion, maintaining hyperglycemia despite elevated basal glucose uptake in skeletal muscle. Rather than reflecting increased gluconeogenesis, this hyperglycemia appears to stem from impaired glucose oxidative disposal; skeletal muscle stores glucose as glycogen instead of oxidizing it, while the heart and brain show persistent, tissue-specific uptake differences. Restoring insulin availability transiently corrects glucose control and reverses stress-induced deficits. Instead of correcting glucose handling, removing excess glucose directly using empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) prevents stress-induced increases in blood glucose. These findings identify a breakdown in endocrine-metabolic coordination underlying metabolic vulnerability in DMD and demonstrate two mechanistically distinct routes, restoring insulin secretion or bypassing it entirely, to restore metabolic resilience under stress.

title: Mantle redox states reveal contrasting styles of late Archean lithospheric subduction
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Lithospheric recycling has operated through most of Earth’s history, likely involving subduction since the late Archean. However, the thermal structure and geometry of such subduction systems remain poorly constrained. Here, we quantify the oxygen fugacity (
                    f
                    O
                    2
                    ) of mantle sources modified by recycled supracrustal materials in the North China Craton. By integrating mantle
                    f
                    O
                    2
                    estimation, thermodynamic simulation of lithospheric structures, and other geological constraints, we infer two styles of lithospheric subduction with contrasting slab-dip angles. The dominant style shows shallow slab-dip angles, a more reduced arc mantle and a thick overriding lithosphere. The subsidiary, localized style exhibits relatively steep slab-dip angles, a more oxidized mantle source and a thinner overriding lithosphere. In contrast to the prevalence of steep subduction on the modern Earth, flat (or shallow) subduction profoundly shaped the distinctive tectonic evolution of the early Earth, whereas the localized development of steep subduction may have enhanced mantle oxidation and strengthened coupling between Earth’s deep interior and surface environments.

title: Unseen but not unheard: Animal-borne audio recorders reveal missing interactions between seabirds and untracked vessels
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Quantifying interactions between marine megafauna and vessels is key to assessing the ecological impacts of commercial fishing and shipping. Automatic identification systems (AIS), by publicly tracking global vessel activities, have enabled animal-vessel interactions to be identified at scale. However, the extent of these interactions is inevitably underestimated due to “unseen” vessels that lack AIS or have gaps in coverage from technical issues or intentional disabling. Using animal-borne audio recorders on three seabird species (northern gannet, Balearic shearwater, and Westland petrel), we investigated whether acoustic detection of vessel sounds could reveal a more complete picture of interactions. We found that a striking proportion of vessel audio detections (gannets, >32%, estimated 57%; shearwaters, >12%, estimated 20%) could not be matched with AIS-tracked vessels, suggesting substantial potential for bycatch risk from unseen fishing. Our approach is computationally lightweight, applicable to pre-existing datasets, and transferrable to non-seabird taxa. Acoustic detection could improve future assessments of animal-vessel interactions and unseen vessel activities to support marine conservation.

title: Atomic-scale visualization and assignment of contaminant adsorption geometries at mineral surfaces
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Directly resolving coexisting adsorption geometries at mineral-water interfaces and assigning them to crystallographic sites remains challenging in environmental geochemistry. Ensemble methods provide population-averaged structural constraints but may obscure minor or similar configurations and do not directly reveal crystallographic registry. Here, we establish an experimentally constrained framework integrating controlled off-axis high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), multislice simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) to resolve crystallographic adsorption registries and corresponding structures. For selenium(IV) adsorption on hematite (001), comparison of apparent selenium positions with multislice simulations accounting for tilt-induced registry shifts supports assignment to iron-iron bridge and oxygen-centered hollow registries. DFT favors monodentate inner-sphere structures compatible with these registries. Extension to lead(II) and uranium(VI) on multiple hematite facets demonstrates the transferability of the off-axis imaging strategy for resolving sparse high-
                    Z
                    interfacial species. This work enables real-space, site-resolved adsorption-structure analysis that complements ensemble-averaged structural methods and provides a basis for mechanistic models of contaminant retention and structure-guided sorbent design.

title: Tuning microswimmer motility by liposome encapsulation: A membrane clutch enables controlled swimming and cargo transport
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Inspired by biology’s use of vesicles for targeted transport, many studies have propelled liposomes with active matter, creating synthetic systems that can be viewed as microscale biohybrid robots. Nevertheless, the underlying motility mechanisms from a hydrodynamic perspective are often unresolved, and reliable velocity control remains challenging. In the present study, we use our previously introduced biohybrid system termed the chlamylipo, in which the motile alga
                    Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
                    is encapsulated within a giant liposome, as a model system to investigate how liposome encapsulation regulates microswimmer motility under controlled perturbations. From a fluid mechanical perspective, we establish a deformation-velocity expression that incorporates liposome radius, beating frequency, and membrane protrusion. We further show that motility can be reversibly switched by incorporating light-responsive lipids, with the liposome acting as a “clutch” that modulates membrane protrusion. To demonstrate its transport function, we further show cargo loading, carrying, and triggered release. These results show that liposome encapsulation can convert a motile microorganism into a controllable carrier, with the membrane acting as a clutch that regulates swimming and, therefore, cargo transport.

title: Global iodine emissions remain near constant over the 21st century
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The reaction between atmospheric ozone and ocean iodide releases gaseous iodine into the atmosphere, destroying ozone and nucleating aerosol particles. The current paradigm is that iodine emissions will substantially increase over this century, with implications for climate, air quality, and human health. Using advanced predictions of ocean iodide concentrations and the iodine emissions function, we re-evaluate this understanding. Rather than increasing through 2100, we find minimal change (−3%) in global iodine emissions compared to present day, predominantly due to a sea surface temperature driven decrease in the iodine emissions function together with relatively unchanged sea surface iodide concentrations. However, emissions increases remain in the critical Arctic region (+143%), resulting in an additional 9 ppbv of springtime surface ozone loss across the region. Our results highlight that predictions of future atmospheric iodine depend on the assumed climate-induced changes in oceanic iodide, in addition to changes in emissions driven by anthropogenic ozone and sea-surface temperature.

title: Signals of rapid genetic change in reef coral over time and following mass mortality
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Future coral reef persistence amidst accelerating climate change depends on rapid adaptive capacity. Sixteen years (2003 to 2019) of genetic data (
                    N
                     = 903) spanning mass mortality events uncovered polygenic signals of evolution and population structure in one Great Barrier Reef coral species (
                    Acropora tenuis
                    ) and a similar but nonsignificant trend in another (
                    Acropora millepora
                    ). Random forest revealed larger genetic shifts postbleaching compared to other time points, which was further supported by critical transitions in 34 years of remotely sensed thermal data (1985 to 2018). Concordant signals across multiple genomic ordinations confirmed significant shifts postbleaching. Specifically, three genetic variants contributed significantly to key random forest splits over time in
                    A. tenuis
                    . Significant genome-wide covariance in allele frequencies suggests shifts due to selection, not drift. This suggests that coral gene pools are changing, and measurable evolution can happen over subdecadal timescales, giving hope for coral resilience amid the ongoing climate crisis. However, we caution against overoptimism, and stress emissions must be urgently reduced.

title: GDF15 impacts chronic kidney disease and associated weight loss through distinct mechanisms
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently accompanied by anorexia, cachexia, and inflammation, which collectively contribute to poor clinical outcomes. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate a pivotal role for growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) in CKD morbidities. Deteriorating renal function and clinical disease status correlates with GDF15 levels in plasma and kidneys of CKD patients. In a mouse CKD model, GDF15 levels are elevated and
                    Gdf15
                    knockout (
                    Gdf15
                    −/−
                    ) mice are partially protected from CKD-induced anorexia and weight loss despite worsening renal function and inflammation. GDF15 receptor
                    Gfral
                    knockout (
                    Gfral
                    −/−
                    ) mice recapitulate these phenotypes. Metabolic cage studies reveal that the weight loss-protection effects are primarily attributed to increased food intake. Intriguingly, pair-fed
                    Gdf15
                    −/−
                    and
                    Gfral
                    −/−
                    mice exhibited phenotypic and molecular divergence. Pair feeding in
                    Gdf15
                    −/−
                    mice reverses loss-of-GDF15’s effect on body weight but does not restore renal functions. In contrast, pair feeding in
                    Gfral
                    −/−
                    mice reverses loss-of-GFRAL’s effect on both body weight and renal function. Transcriptome analysis suggests that GDF15 may act through both GFRAL-dependent mechanisms on food intake and GFRAL-independent mechanisms that primarily modulate inflammation and metabolic pathways. A monoclonal antibody that neutralizes circulating GDF15 markedly restores food intake and preserves body weight, demonstrating the therapeutic potential of targeting GDF15 in CKD-associated weight loss. Together, these findings demonstrate GDF15-GFRAL as a potential therapeutic target for CKD-associated weight loss and suggest GFRAL-dependent, food intake-mediated actions of GDF15 and food intake-independent effects that may contribute to renal inflammation and metabolic regulation.

title: Aclarubicin disrupts RNA polymerase II progression at replication-coupled histone genes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Anthracyclines are effective chemotherapeutic agents that cause DNA and chromatin damage. One member of the anthracyclines, aclarubicin, has gained therapeutic interest due to its ability to kill cancer cells through chromatin-based mechanisms, thus avoiding the off-target effects associated with DNA damage. However, the molecular mechanism of action leading to aclarubicin-induced chromatin damage remains elusive. Here we performed Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and other transcriptional regulators in human cells following aclarubicin treatment. We found that aclarubicin strongly disrupts the replication-coupled histone genes, resulting in a nonproductive accumulation of Pol II transcription machinery at levels exceeding those at other genes. We attribute this sensitivity to the dense Pol II loading and rapid transcription of the histone genes, which intensify the chromatin-disrupting effects of aclarubicin. Together, our findings shed light on the mechanism of aclarubicin as an anticancer drug and point to the replication-coupled histone genes as a target for therapeutic intervention.

title: Bioinspired mucolytic microrods for active mucus penetration and enhanced antibiotic delivery against H. pylori
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Helicobacter pylori
                    infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

title: A programmable cell-free biosensor device for on-demand detection of pathogens and antibiotics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Cell-free systems provide a versatile platform for engineering customizable, gene circuit-based biosensors for decentralized, low-cost molecular diagnostics. Nevertheless, their performance in complex samples is often compromised by matrix interference, necessitating laborious preprocessing that restricts field deployment. Here, we developed a programmable, on-demand, cell-free kit (POCKit) that integrates sample pretreatment with point-of-care detection. The POCKit device comprises a negative pressure storage chamber and a sampling-sensing chamber, which can be connected to a microneedle array or pipette module for sample collection, filtration and target detection via a freeze-dried cell-free molecular reaction network. The POCKit enables detection of
                    Pseudomonas aeruginosa
                    infection in wound exudates, interstitial fluids and artificial sputum within one hour. It also detects tetracycline in food and environmental water, distinguishing tetracycline-spiked samples from negative controls without specialized equipment or tedious preparation. A portable fluorescence imaging box and smartphone application further support real-time signal acquisition and analysis, offering a ready-to-use platform for on-site diagnostics across biomedicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

title: Ubiquitination of USP5 by a bacterial effector inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The intracellular pathogen
                    Legionella pneumophila
                    employs a repertoire of effector proteins to manipulate the host ubiquitin signaling and subvert host immune responses. In this study, we reported that the
                    L. pneumophila
                    effector GobX (Lpg2455) functions as a ubiquitin ligase to target the host deubiquitinase USP5. Ubiquitination of USP5 by GobX inhibits its deubiquitination activity. Furthermore, this ubiquitination enhances the interaction between USP5 and the host E3 ligase MARCHF7, thereby facilitating MARCHF7-dependent ubiquitination of NLRP3. This modification targets NLRP3 for autophagic degradation, ultimately suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages. Our findings uncover a sophisticated strategy in which a bacterial effector hijacks the host ubiquitination machinery to dampen inflammasome signaling.

title: Uterine-derived anisotropic compressive force specifies the anterior-posterior axis orientation in the mouse embryo
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The establishment of the anterior-posterior (A-P) axis is a fundamental process in embryonic patterning. In mice, directional migration of the anterior visceral endoderm (AVE) determines the A-P axis, yet the cues directing migration remain elusive. Here, we show that anisotropic compression directs AVE migration toward the minor-axis end of the deformed embryo, using ex utero culture with controlled compression and in utero pharmacological manipulations of uterine mechanics. This compression induces localized accumulation of basement membrane (BM) components, including COLLAGEN IV, which directs the AVE toward the minor-axis end. Mathematical modeling demonstrates that BM density-dependent AVE-BM adhesion accounts for the observed AVE dynamics. Our findings reveal that the maternal mechanical environment provides directional cues for cell migration, bridging tissue-scale mechanics and biochemical patterning during body axis specification.

title: Probabilistic neural code for subjective value and metacognition in human cortex
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Subjective value underlies many everyday decisions, yet the neural representations supporting these valuations are inherently noisy and subject to uncertainty. Whether humans have metacognitive access to this uncertainty and how this access is supported neurally remain unclear. Here, we provide converging behavioral and neural evidence that subjective value is represented probabilistically in the human brain. Behaviorally, participants’ uncertainty reports tracked trial-by-trial fluctuations in valuation. Neurally, we decoded probability distributions over value from functional magnetic resonance imaging activity in ventromedial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortex, and superior parietal lobe and intraparietal sulcus. Decoded neural uncertainty predicted behaviorally reported uncertainty across trial, item, and individual levels. Moreover, predicting behavioral uncertainty required modeling the covariance structure of population noise. These findings indicate that neural populations jointly encode value and uncertainty, extending probabilistic population coding from perception, working memory to subjective value, and providing a neural basis for metacognitive access to uncertainty in value-based decisions.

title: Spaceflight reshapes Alzheimer’s disease–associated molecular programs in human brain organoids
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Spaceflight provides a unique environment to study neural responses relevant to neurodegenerative diseases. Here, human cortical organoids derived from induced pluripotent stem cells that carry familial Alzheimer’s disease (AD) mutations in APP,
                    PSEN1
                    , and
                    PSEN2
                    were cultivated at the International Space Station alongside Controls for 40 days. Multiomic profiling, integrating transcriptomics and proteomics, revealed a coordinated shift in neuronal and cellular states during spaceflight. Spaceflight was associated with changes in amyloid-β processing and tau phosphorylation, although the magnitude of these responses varied across genetic backgrounds. Pathway analysis identified increased synaptic and neurotransmission-related signatures, particularly those associated with GABA-releasing and glutamatergic signaling. Integrative analysis further revealed convergent programs involving RNA processing, chromatin organization, cytoskeletal dynamics, and cellular stress responses. Proteomic and multiomic analyses also identified changes in RNA binding proteins, including CIRBP, consistent with altered posttranscriptional regulatory networks under spaceflight conditions. These exploratory findings indicate that spaceflight reshapes neuronal regulation in human brain organoids, revealing coordinated molecular responses relevant to AD biology.

title: DAS reveals continuous, multicore architecture of the Alpine Fault, New Zealand
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The Alpine Fault accommodates much of the relative motion between the Australian and Pacific plates in southern New Zealand and is expected to produce large earthquakes in coming decades. How slip evolves and what ground motions are produced during the next rupture are expected to depend strongly on the continuity of principal slip zones and overall fault width. Despite extensive study, the along-strike structure of the fault and its continuity across segment boundaries remain poorly constrained. Here, we use distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) along a 30-kilometer fiber-optic array crossing the Alpine Fault to record fault-zone guided waves (FZGWs) from local earthquakes. The FZGW observations, supported by numerical modeling and passive seismic imaging, reveal up to six narrow (∼10 meters) fault cores embedded within a 200-meter-wide low-velocity zone interpreted as the fault’s inner damage zone. The principal fault core feature persists for ∼180 kilometers along strike between the Central and South Westland segments, crossing a pronounced geometric and kinematic boundary. The inferred damage zone width is consistent with empirical scaling for large-displacement faults. These results demonstrate that DAS can resolve fault-zone architecture at previously inaccessible scales and bridge geological and geophysical inferences, providing constraints on fault continuity, slip localization, and the potential for multisegment rupture in mature plate-boundary systems.

title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4
                    +
                    tumor cells, with CD8
                    +
                    T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand–receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8
                    +
                    T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8
                    +
                    T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8
                    +
                    T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8
                    +
                    T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8
                    +
                    T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4–GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

title: A precipitation threshold delineates contrasting controls on global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Nitrogen fertilization is a major driver of soil acidification globally, yet its independent effects on soil pH and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly resolved. Here we isolate the contribution of nitrogen fertilization by compiling the largest paired experimental dataset to date, consisting of 3564 paired soil pH observations under control and nitrogen fertilization treatments across seven major ecosystem types worldwide. By constructing robust machine-learning models, we predict global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization (pH_T) and quantify fertilization-associated pH change under a standardized hypothetical fertilization scenario. Under this scenario, we estimate that 96.27% of global soils undergo acidification, with a mean pH decline of 0.34 units. Critically, we identify a precipitation threshold at ∼900 mm year
                    −1
                    that separates two distinct regimes in the relationship between precipitation and pH_T: climate-driven leaching and buffering in drier regions versus soil-mediated internal regulation in humid regions. This threshold demonstrates that the association between precipitation and pH_T is not uniform across the global precipitation gradient but varies markedly among hydroclimatic regions. Our results provide a global outlook on soil pH responses to nitrogen fertilization, supporting acidification risk early warning, precision fertilizer management, and sustainable agricultural development.

title: Arctic forcing of European spring productivity and agricultural yields linked to Barents Sea ice loss
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Arctic sea ice loss reshapes midlatitude climate, yet its cascading impacts on terrestrial carbon cycling and food security remain unclear. Barents Sea ice area (BSIA) has experienced the Arctic’s fastest decline. Using four decades of satellite observations, agricultural statistics, and Earth system model (ESM) simulations, we identify late-winter BSIA as a key driver of European spring productivity. Interannual BSIA reductions substantially enhance gross primary productivity (GPP) and raise national wheat yields by up to 16.5% in Eastern Europe, a global breadbasket. Reanalysis and model experiments reveal that reduced BSIA alters large-scale circulation through stratosphere-troposphere coupling, wave–mean flow interactions, and Rossby wave propagation. Anomalous subsidence drives adiabatic and radiative warming; cyclonic flow strengthens warm-air advection, together alleviating thermal constraints on photosynthesis. Although most ESMs capture atmospheric teleconnections, they systematically underestimate productivity responses due to underrepresented GPP-temperature sensitivity. BSIA decline accounts for approximately half of the four-decade increase in Eastern European productivity, highlighting an overlooked Arctic forcing of midlatitude carbon dynamics.

title: A flexible fiber–based artificial chemical postsynapse
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Most artificial synapses, which are designed to communicate with biological neural systems and exhibit neuron-like functions, rely primarily on electrical signals. Biotic-abiotic neural interfaces that use artificial synapses to communicate with biological synapses via chemical neurotransmitters while exhibiting synaptic plasticity are of great interest. Here, we present an artificial chemical postsynapse that directly interfaces with biological systems through dopamine (DA) neurotransmitters and demonstrates synaptic plasticity–like behavior. The artificial postsynapse of a flexible fiber–based organic electrochemical transistor (F-OECT) with a capacitive-like charging gate electrode, which combines volumetric charge storage and DA-sensing functionalities, can detect pulsatile DA release and transduce these sensing signals with plasticity-like behavior. The F-OECT synapse emulates key synaptic functions observed in biological synapses by responding to pulse-like DA release from dopaminergic cells. We also implanted fiber-based artificial postsynapses into a mouse brain to study their basic interaction with DA release and to evaluate biocompatibility.

title: Historical evidence that wildfire frequency modulates debris-flow hazards through sediment-supply limitation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Southern California is an epicenter of postwildfire debris flows. In this region, steep topography, frequent fire, heavy rainstorms, and large populations along the wildland-urban interface conspire to produce costly debris flows. Wildfire frequency in the region has tripled in recent decades, causing concern about escalating debris-flow hazards. Here, we investigate how wildfire frequency affects the magnitude of postfire erosion by analyzing long-term debris basin records. We identify two contrasting erosional styles. In steep catchments, erosion exhibits a binge-purge behavior: Erosion for 3 years following fire exceeds background rates by ∼17×. In contrast, in low-sloping, soil-mantled catchments, sediment export following fire only exceeds background rates by ∼1.5×. Critically, in the steep catchments, debris-flow volumes decline when wildfires recur more frequently than the ∼30-year interval characteristic of the past century. This observation suggests a sediment-supply limitation in which more frequent wildfire may reduce, rather than amplify, some of Southern California’s most severe debris-flow hazards.

title: Ion‐Pair Mediation Enables Low‐Viscosity, Nonflammable Ternary Hybrid Electrolytes for High‐Voltage Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have garnered attention as promising energy storage devices owing to their intrinsic safety. However, the practical energy density of AZMBs is severely constrained by the narrow electrochemical window and sluggish kinetics inherent to conventional concentrated or viscous aqueous electrolytes. To address these limitations, a ternary hybrid system comprising a Zn(OTf)
                    2
                    /LiOTf dual‐salt matrix and low‐volume (5 vol.%) 1‐ethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (EMIMTFSI, abbreviated as EMT) ionic liquid is constructed. In the ternary system, EMIM
                    +
                    ‐TFSI
                    −
                    /OTf
                    −
                    ion pairs reconstruct the hydrogen‐bond network of the dual‐salt framework, thereby reducing bulk viscosity and broadening the electrochemical stability window to 2.76 V at low total salt concentrations. More importantly, these ion pairs undergo adsorption‐reduction‐anchoring to form an inner inorganic/outer organic bilayer, where OTf
                    −
                    /TFSI
                    −
                    decomposition generates a robust fluoride‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that subsequently anchors EMIM
                    +
                    as a dynamic cationic shield. Consequently, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells achieve an outstanding lifespan of 3215 h at 1 mA cm
                    −2
                    . Zn//MnO
                    2
                    ‐CNT battery demonstrates 88.21% capacity retention after 1100 cycles at 1 A g
                    −1
                    within a high‐voltage range (0.8–2.0 V), and Zn//LiMn
                    2
                    O
                    4
                    battery exhibits a high discharge plateau of 1.86 V v s. Zn. This work offers a promising electrolyte design strategy for high‐voltage and long‐cycle‐life AZMBs.

title: Ion‐Pair Decoupler Tunes Solvation Chemistry for Room‐Temperature Polymer Electrolytes With Built‐In Flame Retardancy
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Solid‐state polymer electrolytes for high‐energy lithium‐metal batteries are severely constrained by low room‐temperature ionic conductivity. However, mainstream approaches focus on regulating the aggregate structure and flexibility of polymer chains while neglecting the ionic solvation microenvironment, which caps ionic conductivity gains at a marginal level. Here, an innovative ion‐pair decoupling strategy is proposed to reshape the Li
                    +
                    solvation chemistry within polymer matrices and to facilitate rapid ionic conduction. The ion‐pair decoupler, diethyl phosphoramidate, promotes the dissociation of lithium salt into a configuration dominated by solvent‐separated ion pairs by coordinating with Li
                    +
                    via its electron‐rich P = O groups and anchoring TFSI
                    ‒
                    through hydrogen bond donors. Consequently, the ionic conductivity of the engineered electrolyte increases 24.6‐fold at 25°C. Li symmetric cells achieve stable cycling over 850 h, and Li||LiFePO
                    4
                    cells deliver a high‐capacity retention rate of 96.5% after 400 cycles at 25°C. Furthermore, the designed electrolyte exhibits excellent self‐extinguishing flame‐retardant properties by combining gas‐phase radical scavenging and condensed‐phase char‐forming mechanisms. Thus, a single molecular design simultaneously serves as an ion‐pair decoupler and an intrinsic flame retardant, establishing solvation‐chemistry tuning as a new paradigm for safe, room‐temperature solid polymer electrolytes.

title: In Situ Formation of Inorganic‐Rich Interphase via SiO2 Additive for High‐Performance Sodium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents

ABSTRACT

title: Unified Grain‐Boundary and Electrode‐Interface Engineering Enables High‐Performance Magnesium‐Based Thermoelectrics

ABSTRACT
                  
                    High‐performance thermoelectric devices require not only intrinsically efficient materials but also minimized transport losses across multiple interfaces during device integration. However, internal transport interfaces and external electrode contacts are typically optimized independently, creating a persistent challenge in translating material‐level advances into device‐level performance. Here we establish a unified interface engineering strategy in Bi‐rich Mg
                    3

                    , Nb‐rich internal interfaces regulate grain‐boundary carrier transport, while Nb foils provide chemically stable and low‐resistance electrode contacts. First‐principles calculations and atomic‐scale characterization reveal that the Bi‐rich composition suppresses extensive Nb‐related reactions while enabling electronically favorable confined interfaces. Nb incorporation increases the weighted mobility to 315.6 cm

                    2

                    with p‐type MgAgSb enables Mg‐based thermoelectric modules with a conversion efficiency of 3.8% at Δ

This work establishes a general interface design principle for thermoelectrics, demonstrating that interface modifiers for bulk transport optimization can also serve as electrode‐contact materials to bridge the gap between high‐performance materials and practical devices.

title: In Situ Polymerized Interfaces Enable Robust and High‐Performance Dry‐Coating Electrodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Dry‐coating electrode technology eliminates the use of toxic N‐methyl‐2‐pyrrolidone and offers a promising route for sustainable battery manufacturing. However, its practical implementation remains limited by the weak interfacial mechanics among rigid cathode particles, polytetrafluoroethylene nanofibers, and conductive carbon additives. These fragile interfaces reduce mechanical robustness and interfacial stability, thereby compromising both processability and electrochemical performance. Here, we report an in situ polymerization strategy using a polymerizable deep eutectic liquid additive, which forms an adhesive polymer network upon photopolymerization, thereby reinforcing contact among electrode components and improving electrode robustness. The resulting dry‐coating LiNi
                    0.8
                    Co
                    0.1
                    Mn
                    0.1
                    O
                    2
                    (NCM811) electrodes exhibit a 55% increase in elongation at break and deliver a reversible specific capacity of 121 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 5 C with a mass loading of 10 mg cm
                    −2
                    . A 3.77 Ah Li||NCM811 pouch cell achieves maximum cell‐level energy and power densities of 412 Wh kg
                    −1
                    and 574 W kg
                    −1
                    , respectively. In addition, a 0.60 Ah graphite||NCM811 pouch cell retains 70% of its capacity after 870 cycles. Our results establish in situ polymerization as a viable route for mechanically robust, high‐performance dry‐coating electrodes.
